Arsenal confirmed this week that they have shelved plans for a major expansion of the Emirates Stadium after Arteta is believed to have expressed concern over the disruption that would have been caused by any temporary move. His side face Leeds on Saturday as they attempt to bounce back from a surprise 3-0 defeat at Brighton before the international break that ended the champions’ 100% start to the new campaign.

Sports.title: Portuguese authorities took 83 days to tell Rui Pinto his witness protection was ending
Sports.content:
Portuguese authorities kept Rui Pinto in the dark for almost three months about their decision to end his status as a protected witness and notified the Manchester City whistleblower 10 days before it was due to expire, it can be revealed.

According to documents seen by the Guardian, the special security programmes commission (CPES), which oversees Portugal’s witness protection programme, met on 8 and 9 July to discuss Pinto’s case. It concluded that the threat level against him was low and that the special protection measures were no longer warranted.

Yet it was not until 30 September that Pinto, who has been a protected witness since 2020 after agreeing to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files gathered before his arrest, was informed of the decision – 83 days after it had been made.

With 10 days’ notice, Pinto was left with little time to address a number of immediate issues. He needs to find somewhere safe to live and establish a way of supporting himself in a new location, while avoiding contact with family members.

The Guardian contacted the CPES on two occasions seeking details of the criteria and evidence used to determine that Pinto’s protection should be withdrawn. On Wednesday, the commission was also asked to explain the 83-day gap between its decision and the notification. None of the inquiries received a response.

On 30 September, the day Pinto was informed his protected-witness status was coming to an end, the Premier League’s guilty verdict against City, which had been confirmed 24 hours earlier, was dominating headlines around the world. The authorities stood by the decision reached nearly three months earlier despite protestations from Pinto and his lawyers that he fears for his life.

Pinto entered Portugal’s protection programme after cooperating with the country’s justice authorities. His revelations have subsequently been used by judicial, tax and sporting authorities across Europe, including the Premier League’s investigation into City’s alleged financial irregularities. Pinto’s lawyers argue that the authorities should take into account his cooperation with the justice system and the continuing risks associated with his disclosures before ending his protection.

Mounting pressure appears to have prompted a rethink. Last Saturday Portugal’s justice minister, Rita Alarcão Júdice, was questioned by journalists about the decision. She said the authorities would review Pinto’s case and promised to respond by Saturday, the date on which his protection is due to end.

“I have received various requests and we are examining them very carefully,” Júdice said. “If there has been any irregularity, or if any procedure was not handled as it should have been, that will, of course, be taken into consideration.”

The Guardian understands that, as it first reported, Pinto remains willing to cooperate with British authorities in the City case and in other investigations stemming from his findings. He handed over millions of documents to investigators in France, which can now be shared with other nations – including the UK – under international cooperation and bilateral ties.

Pinto’s lawyer, Francisco Teixeira da Mota, told the Guardian an appeal against the decision would be filed this week. “The most shocking thing is the fact that he wasn’t heard before the decision was made,” he said. “It’s something that goes against the European court of human rights.”

In a press release last week, Pinto’s defence team called the decision “an act of state terrorism”. Their outrage has intensified after they learnedtheir client had been kept in the dark for almost three months. “It says a lot,” Da Mota added.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Chelsea set to miss a month of next WSL season due to Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The Women’s Super League will face major disruption next season due to the Club World Cup, with Arsenal and Chelsea likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month.

The Guardian revealed last week that the inaugural Women’s Club World Cup is set to be awarded to the US, with transatlantic travel to cause additional problems for European sides, while the proposed dates of 5-30 January will clash directly with the WSL.

Fifa has yet to confirm the qualification criteria for the Club World Cup but the Guardian has learned Arsenal are guaranteed to be involved as 2025 Champions League winners and Chelsea are likely to join them, although they would lose their place if Manchester City win this season’s Champions League. Based on this season’s schedule, an extended run in the Club World Cup would mean the two English clubs missing up to four WSL match weeks plus the fourth round of the FA Cup, playing havoc with the fixture list and causing major congestion at the end of the season.

Uefa will be granted places for six clubs: five to qualify automatically and one to take part in a six-team qualifier before the tournament, with the three highest-ranked clubs joining 13 automatic qualifiers to form a 16-team competition. While the process has still to be ratified by the Fifa council, it is understood Uefa’s spots will be given to the Champions League winners between 2024 and 2027 – currently Barcelona as the two-time champions and Arsenal, with this season’s title still up for grabs – topped up by the highest-ranked clubs in Uefa’s Champions League coefficient table.

Chelsea are third in that table for the current four-year cycle, behind Barcelona and Lyon with a 17-point lead over fourth-placed Bayern Munich, and cannot be caught. Based on the current rankings, Bayern and Wolfsburg are next in line to qualify, although the latter have not qualified for this season’s Champions League and will not accumulate additional points, so are likely to be overhauled by Real Madrid or Paris Saint-Germain. Fifa plans to cap the number of participants from each country at two, so City winning the Champions League would cost Chelsea their place.

The WSL declined to comment as it has yet to be told of Fifa’s plans for the tournament, but sources conceded its impact is likely to prove challenging. The WSL has a winter break, which is scheduled for 21 December to 10 January this season, and although that could be pushed back slightly, aligning it with the Club World Cup is not viewed as practical due to the congested calendar.

As well as creating a lopsided ­season, moving the winter break would result in a backlog of WSL fixtures during the period when the Champions League knockout stage begins at the beginning of February. The issue of fixture congestion is a growing area of concern in the women’s game and 2028 will be particularly problematic due to the Olympic football tournament taking place in Los Angeles in August, just before the start of the European domestic season.

The International Olympic Committee has expanded women’s football to 16 nations at the 2028 Games, and unlike the men’s version which is restricted to players under 23 with three overage exceptions, senior internationals are permitted to take part.

Fifa’s imposition of the Club World Cup in the middle of the European season has exacerbated the problem, and last month European Leagues, a lobby group, extended its legal complaint to the European Commission about the world governing body’s alleged “abuse of power and dominant position” to include the women’s game.

Sports.title: Kieran McKenna lands new job five months after sudden Ipswich departure
Sports.content:
Kieran McKenna has returned to football by starting work as a technical observer for UEFA, months after his Ipswich departure.

The Northern Irishman made the surprise decision to leave Portman Road in June after guiding the Tractor Boys back to the Premier League.

3 McKenna has been out of football for the past four months after leaving Ipswich Credit: Getty

McKenna had been linked with the Fulham vacancy but instead chose to take a break from football after five years with the Tractor Boys.

During his time at Ipswich, he secured five promotions but decided to quit in June to spend more time with his family.

And the 40-year-old is now back in the game in a different capacity, having taken up the role with European football's governing body.

Having taken on the role of technical observer, McKenna will now be tasked with analysing Champions League games, and selecting the Player of the Match.

Those in the job also produce a report after each game, providing strategic and tactical feedback which can be used by coaches.

McKenna will also help choose team, player and goal of the season along with other observers.

His first shift in his new role will see him observe Shakhtar Donetsk's clash with AEK Athens next Wednesday, hosted at Chelsea's home Stamford Bridge.

McKenna discusses new role

Discussing his latest gig with the Guardian, McKenna revealed this is the perfect way for him to continue learning before he makes a return to management.

He said: “I wanted to give myself the best possibility to learn before taking on the next challenge."

He added: “I’m always going to want to be somewhere where I can improve players, play attacking football and win games.

3 McKenna is now looking to hone his analytical skills as a technical observer Credit: Getty

“But beyond that I’m a manager who wants to enjoy having that connection with a club, a community, trying to build something memorable.”

McKenna isn't the first high-profile name to try their hand as a technical observer for UEFA.

Last season's Champions League saw ex-Tottenham boss Ange Postecoglou, former England manager Sir Gareth Southgate and then Portugal boss Roberto Martinez on the panel.

What next for McKenna?

In the same interview, McKenna shed light on his stance on a return to management, revealing he had been keen to leave Ipswich on a high.

The Tractor Boys were 12th in League One when McKenna took over and his heroics in guiding the club to back-to-back promotions to the Championship and Premier League saw him regularly tipped for other vacancies.

With Michael Carrick enduring a difficult start to the season at Manchester United, talkSPORT's Alan Brazil recently named McKenna as a potential replacement if the former were to be sacked.

3 McKenna decided to take a break from football after guiding Ipswich back to the Premier League Credit: PA

On his Ipswich departure, McKenna said: “I had a lot of different opportunities to leave, could have left in many different circumstances really.

“But I was always aware I wanted to depart in the best way possible, with the club on a high, back in the Premier League and with a great chance to build for what will hopefully be a really successful period.

“It was a really special opportunity at Ipswich and you want to do that again in your career. But you have to be ready to come in somewhere and get some short-term success as well.

“What’s right for me, after two decades coaching, might be different for a manager who only stopped playing three years ago.

“I want to enjoy the time we have now, take this period to reflect and be in the best position I can for the next role.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta urged to make major change to starting XI for Arsenal vs Leeds
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has been urged to start Viktor Gyokeres against Leeds United on Saturday.

Arsenal fan and content creator Joel Beya wants to see the Sweden international start the game at the Emirates Stadium, live on talkSPORT.



2 Gyokeres has firmly been second choice at Arsenal this season Credit: Getty

Kai Havertz is an injury doubt for the game having limped off during the international break.

And that could see Gyokeres handed a first Premier League start of the season.

In the opening five top-flight games so far, Gyokeres has played just 29 minutes and not started.



However, Beya wants to see Gyokeres get the nod to lead the line, saying on talkSPORT Breakfast, he said: "I think he's going to start.

"If you look at his record against Leeds last season. He's got three goals - two at home and one away, and he's on form at the moment.



"I have seen people say that Mikel Merino should be starting. I love Merino, I think he's the best finisher at the club but for the good of his confidence, he has to start.

"If he can't start against Leeds with the way he's performed during the international break, then it's a signal that his time could be up."



Green shoots

The 28-year-old might not have scored for Arsenal this season yet, but he enjoyed a very good international break.

Gyokeres played all four of Sweden's Nations League games, and he scored in every match which saw Graham Potter's side collected ten points from a possible 12.

But some still aren't sold on Gyokeres' use to Arsenal, although talkSPORT's Andy Brassell is certainly not unconvinced.

2 Gyokeres has 21 goals in 60 games for Arsenal Credit: Getty



Brassell told talkSPORT.com: "We could talk about his struggles. What opportunity has he really had so far? I mean, we're looking at what, half an hour's worth of play? Really?

"I mean, I don't think anyone can realistically turn around and say, he's not good enough off the back of half an hour's Premier League football so far this season? To me, that seems ridiculous. To me, I thought he had a very acceptable first season in the Premier League.

"And I know people look at him and say, ‘Oh, we expected more.’

To me, he did exactly what he was meant to do last season. He provided them with a different option up front, and he was part of a team that came close to winning it all.

"And of course, got the Premier League over the line, which is the most important thing. So, for people to be talking like he's some sort of deadweight, I find a bit ludicrous, to be perfectly honest. Now, I don't know what people are expecting.



"If they're expecting him to replicate his Sporting numbers in the Premier League, because we're going to be waiting a long time for that to happen. But I think he is someone who, I think, you'd hope that he increases his output over the next little while.

"But I don't know if part of it is, in a summer when they went for Vinicius, that you think, OK, this is where we are as Arsenal now. We're going for elite ready-made players.

"And maybe there's not the patience to see Gyokeres get to that point. I've made the comparison before with Didier Drogba, who, if you compare his first couple of seasons in the Premier League with what Gyokeres has done in his first season, it is quite comparable, actually.

"No one even thinks about Drogba's first couple of seasons in the Premier League now. Obviously he was a year or two younger.

But I think writing him off this quickly to me seems a bit daft when he has had a decent first season.



"Now I realise that part of the debate is informed by Arsenal being at such a high level really for the last season and a bit. I don't think anything that he's done on international break would really change people's opinion.

"The only way he would change people's minds is by scoring big goals in games for Arsenal in the Premier League and big games in the Champions League. That is the only thing that is going to do it. I think with the opportunity he will get there.

"But say if Arsenal were to keep him for the next two seasons and he scores goals at the same sort of lick that he did in his first season, I don't think he'd look back at that and think that's a really dreadful failure."

Sports.title: Former Premier League player retires due to health issue he kept a secret for years
Sports.content:
Former Premier League player retires due to health issue he kept a secret for years

Former West Ham and Crystal Palace midfielder Cheikhou Kouyate has retired from football after battling with a secret heart condition.

The Senegalese made 296 appearances over a decade in the Premier League, with Nottingham Forest his last club in England back in 2024.

3 Kouyate made 129 Premier League appearances for West Ham Credit: Getty

After a year out of football following his departure from the City Ground, Kouyate most recently played for Turkish side Amedspor.

He spent just a few months there after joining in the summer of 2025, making eight appearances before leaving in January.

Kouyate then almost returned to former club Anderlecht this summer, but was advised to stop playing as he revealed this was due to a heart defect he had been dealing with for his entire career.

Kouyate reveals secret health battle

Speaking to Senegalese channel Walf TV, Kouyate said: “I suffered from this heart problem since birth. I played with it.

“In England, it was monitored every six months. I had medical check-ups at West Ham, Crystal Palace, and Nottingham Forest. Every time I had the tests, the problem reappeared.

“The doctors always pointed out the problem to me, but I took responsibility myself.

“I signed the insurance papers stating that anything that might happen to me would be my responsibility.

“Anderlecht called me [in the summer] to play there and also to start training as a coach. But after the medical examination, the doctor asked me to stop playing football.”

While Kouyate suffered from several minor injuries during his career he did not appear to miss any action because of his heart issue.

And the ex-Senegal international revealed this was because his condition would only flare up in certain circumstances.

3 Kouyate enjoyed a fruitful Premier League career despite concealing a heart condition Credit: Getty

He explained: “The problem is at high altitude. If I play in the heat, it hurts terribly, during and after matches.

“It feels like a side stitch, for about five minutes, and then it goes away. When it happens, after the match, I get painful cramps. After 24 hours, it stops.

“I never said anything. I didn’t want to be forced to stop early.

“I never told my family, not even the national team doctors. They didn’t know about my problem.”

Kouyate's versatility saw him become a reliable presence during his ten-year stay in the Premier League.

Capable of playing in both midfield and at centre-back, he first moved to English football when he joined West Ham from Anderlecht in 2014.

3 Kouyate helped Nottingham Forest to secure Premier League safety in his two years at the City Ground Credit: Getty

Four years in east London followed, where Kouyate was a virtual ever-present and made 147 appearances overall, scoring 15 goals.

In 2018, the versatile star moved across London to join Crystal Palace, spending four years at Selhurst Park where he featured 141 times.

Newly-promoted Nottingham Forest came calling in 2022 as they sought top-flight experience, and Kouyate provided exactly that to help them to establish themselves in the Premier League.

A move to Leeds was mooted after he left Forest upon the expiry of his contract in 2024 before an undisclosed medical issue put a stop to this, and he instead spent a year out of football before eventually enjoying his last spell in Turkey with Amedspor.

On the international stage, Kouyate earned 92 caps for Senegal and represented his country at both the 2018 and 2022 World Cups.

Arguably the peak of his international career came in 2022, when the midfielder tasted Arica Cup of Nations glory in Cameroon.

Sports.title: Jarell Quansah could make Premier League return as three clubs circle
Sports.content:
Jarell Quansah could make Premier League return as three clubs circle

Jarell Quansah could return to the Premier League next summer, with Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea reportedly interested.

After leaving Anfield to join Bayer Leverkusen in 2025, Quansah has become a hot property after impressing in Germany.

5 Quansah's continued strong form has seen him earn nine England caps over the last year Credit: Getty

German outlet BILD recently reported that European giants Real Madrid have identified the England defender as a transfer target.

And there could now be a potential transfer tug-of-war emerging over Quansah, with a trio of English clubs now said to be keen.

According to Sky Germany, Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal are all interested in bringing the 23-year-old back to the Premier League.

The Gunners' interest comes after BILD's report claimed Quansah was the subject of a failed £55m bid this summer, with talkSPORT reporting at the time that discussions had taken place over a move.

And while the Englishman could have a choice between three options back home or the Santiago Bernabeu next summer, one club could have the edge in the negotiations.

Liverpool's upper hand

Liverpool remain in the driving seat should Quansah leave Leverkusen.

The Reds inserted a £59.5m buy-back clause for their academy star as part of Quansah’s Leverkusen deal.

The Merseyside club have until June 2027 to activate the clause.

Liverpool could be in the market for a centre-back next summer with captain Virgil van Dijk’s contract set to expire.

Quansah came through the Reds' academy and made his senior debut in a 2-1 win over Newcastle in August 2023.

5 Quansah's last act at Liverpool came in lifting the club's 20th top-flight title Credit: Getty

5 While Liverpool have the upper hand in any Quansah negotiations, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta could push for his signature again next summer Credit: Getty

He went on to make 58 appearances for the Reds, scoring three times.

Quansah on top form

Quansah has seen his stock rise since leaving Liverpool in 2025, having made his senior England debut and featured in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad over the past year.

He has remained in favour with the Three Lions, starting in three of their four Nations League games in the recent international break.

The Leverkusen star played the full 90 minutes of the defeat to Spain, ahead of former Liverpool teammate Trent Alexander-Arnold, before starting in the 7-0 thumping of Croatia and a 3-0 victory over Czechia.

And at club level, Quansah has been in superb form for Leverkusen after joining the club in a record £30million switch in 2025.

Quansah has been deployed as both a centre-back and right-back, offering much-needed versatility to the Bundesliga outfit.

5 Quansah has quickly become a key figure for Bayern Leverkusen after joining the club from Liverpool in 2025 Credit: AFP

Quansah tipped for homecoming

With some huge names circling over Quansah's signature, European football expert Andy Brassell admitted a return to Liverpool is a real possibility, with Leverkusen unlikely to stand in the player's way.

He told talkSPORT: “If Liverpool activate the buyback, I don't think they'll [Leverkusen] be disappointed because it's quite a high figure."

Highlighting his quality, Brassell added: “If you've got Quansah in the team, you've got enormous versatility. Because he's someone who is good with the ball at his feet, so he can add to the attack."

Brassell also insisted Quansah could have a real opportunity to showcase his abilities in the Europa League this term.

Leverkusen are once again competing in Europe's second-tier competition after missing out on Champions League qualification, and launching a serious title bid would boost the defender's image.

Making this point, Brassell admitted this could well pave the way for a Liverpool return, where Quansah could partner Jeremy Jacquet in defence should Van Dijk leave at the end of his contract next summer.

5 Jacquet has impressed this term since making his £55m move to Liverpool Credit: Getty

He continued: “I imagine if Leverkusen have a good season, do well in the Europa League - remember they were finalists last time they were in it [in 2024], the competition is indisputably weaker now - he'll get plenty of opportunities to show how good he is.

“And that will open up the opportunity [to move], not just of Liverpool possibly buying him - maybe we're looking at that.

"Maybe we're looking at a Jacquet/Quansah double act this time next year, I don't know.

“But I would be amazed if he has a good season, and Leverkusen have a good season, if he's not on the block to get sold, and he's not piquing the interest of more clubs than Liverpool at the end of the season.”

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham player announces shock bid to stand against Gianni Infantino in FIFA election
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega is intending to stand as a candidate for the FIFA presidency next year.

The 55-year-old is planning to challenge Gianni Infantino to lead FIFA with huge pressure on the current president to resign and not stand.



3 Vega spent four years in north London with Tottenham and now wants to be one of the most powerful men in the world

And Vega is intending to take on his fellow Swiss national, with the election happening in Moroccan capital Rabat on March 18.

So far, Vega is the first person to publicly confirm their intention to stand against Infantino, with deadlines for candidacy ending on November 18.

Speaking in a statement released on Wednesday, he said: "I am standing to reunite the global football family, deliver genuine and lasting reform, modernise FIFA for the 21st Century, restore stability and credibility, and rebuild the trust that our game urgently needs.



"I am standing because my life has prepared me to serve the game.

"Football does not belong to presidents, confederations or administrators. Football is greater than any position, any individual or any institution.

"It is the people's game and belongs to everyone: the players, coaches, referees, supporters, volunteers, clubs, leagues, associations and communities that give football its life.



"It belongs to every child discovering the game, every professional carrying the hopes of a nation, and the billions of supporters whose passion makes football the world's game.

"Football must always come first. Yet for too long, division has fractured our football family.



"The current leadership has demoralised the game. Weak governance has damaged FIFA's credibility and eroded trust across the global football family. We must stop this conflict from escalating.

"Ego-driven battles within football administration must never be allowed to damage those who matter most: the players, coaches, referees and supporters around the world. They are not responsible for these conflicts. They deserve better.

3 Infantino's failed plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup has seen confidence in him collapse Credit: AFP

"Football is in the emergency room, on life support. We cannot wait any longer. FIFA needs a new direction and fundamental reform. We must reunite the football family, restore trust, bring stability and modernise FIFA's governance. This requires decisive change - not cosmetic adjustments."



Infantino's future

The 56-year-old confirmed in September that he fully intended to run again for FIFA president.

And before the World Cup, he was expected to be re-elected totally unopposed.

But after he tried and failed to come up with a plan to sell off parts of the World Cup, it led to a large scale rejection of the plan and many countries withdrew their support for Infantino.

UEFA were particularly scathing in the criticism of their former employee and are contemplating a vote of no confidence.



And after threats of FIFA events being boycotted, Infantino abandoned his plans, but he still intends to run again ahead of the 77th FIFA Congress in March.

3 Infantino also buckled to political pressure from Donald Trump during the World Cup to allow Folarin Balogun play for the USA against Belgium despite being sent off in the match before Credit: Getty

In a statement from FIFA, Infantino's intentions were confirmed.

"The FIFA President announced in April that he will stand for re-election in 2027," it read.

"Of course, nothing has changed. Mr Infantino will be standing for re-election."



What are the requirements to stand as FIFA president?

Vega might well have announced his intention to run as president, but there is an awful lot more to it than just that.

There are three key things that any candidate must fulfil to have any chance of standing.

The first is that they need to have worked a role in football for two of the last five years.

At least five separate Football Associations also have to endorse the individual, and finally there are a set of FIFA integrity checks.

Sports.title: Man City scandal could topple Andy Burnham as prime minister, says football club owner
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham has been warned his implication in the Manchester City case could cost him his position as prime minister.

Burnham has come under scrutiny following his public comments on City's seismic ruling after an independent commission found the club guilty on all charges of breaches of Premier League financial rules.



4 Burnham was Mayor of Greater Manchester as recently as June, before becoming prime minister in July Credit: AFP

The Premier League giants have since appealed against the verdict, with their punishment yet to be decided.

City are adjudged to have inflated their revenue by more than £900million by disguising owner funding as sponsorship over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

During this time, City won eight trophies including three top-flight titles.



talkSPORT understands the club intend to argue that sponsorship deals were propped up by the Abu Dhabi government, not Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) and consequently owner Sheikh Mansour.

Burnham's 'concern' over Man City

Burnham has come under fire after he insisted he would be 'really concerned' if City's owners had to sell up, with the Independent Football Regulator able to strip the owners of their licence to own the club once the disciplinary process is over.



The UK prime minister was the mayor of Greater Manchester from 2017 to 2026, and appeared to voice his support of City's owners.

Burnham told the BBC: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

“I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn’t just put into the Etihad [Stadium] and the campus around it but also into the city.”



He added: "I can’t intervene more in the process, it would be wrong for me to do that, it would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail.

"But obviously it’s ongoing, and because it’s still contested by Manchester City then I think it’s right that I don’t say much more.”

4 Burnham has previously liaised with Manchester City's owners, the Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) Credit: AFP

Burnham's comments sparked accusations of political interference in the independent investigation process.



City owners ADUG have poured hundreds of millions of pounds into the city of Manchester during Burnham’s tenure as mayor - namely investing in a joint property venture between Manchester city council and ADUG, called ManchesterLife, which was first founded in 2014.

Downing Street was later forced to clarify the Prime Minister’s remarks, stressing that the findings against City were 'serious' and that the process must be respected.

'Chance this topples the Prime Minister'

Journalist and co-owner of Mexican top-flight club Queretaro FC, Ed Maylon, has warned that Burnham's comments on Man City could land him in major trouble if their guilty verdict stands.

Maylon highlighted Burnham's possible dealings with ADUG in property development in Manchester as a potential concern.



He told talkSPORT: “I don't think states should be allowed to own football clubs. I don't think that's even an extreme stance. I just don't think nation states should be allowed.

4 Man City are fighting for their Premier League existence amid their ongoing appeal with any number of sanctions possible Credit: Getty

“And when anyone asks why, you just point around you - look at this absolute mess we're in.

“My probably extreme view on the Man City case, I think there's a non-zero chance that this topples the Prime Minister.



“I just saw the way that Burnham reacted to that Man City news and the things he didn't say. And it worries me about what went down in Manchester around the property deals."

While Burnham cited his previous defence of his club, Everton, when they were punished for PSR breaches in 2023 as an example of his consistency over the City saga, Maylon disagreed.

He continued: “Burnham has been [going]: ‘I’m the Everton fan. I'm the everyman football supporter, I am that guy.’

“He's got a lot of historic tweets taking the mickey out of Chelsea [for their historical rule breaches] or whichever club it happens to be.



4 An avid Everton fan, Burnham has previously weighed in on other footballing debates including the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches Credit: Getty

"You can't suddenly turn around and be like, ‘Well, yes, this is bad, but also Abu Dhabi has been a great friend to the UK in like real estate development, the economy’ - that doesn't play.

“I know you’re prime minister now, and I know it's different, but I look at that and I think he has not handled it well, and it worries me why he's not handled it well.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola tipped to make return to Etihad Stadium this month
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola has been tipped to appear at the Etihad Stadium for Manchester City's Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain next week.

This prediction has been made by Spanish football expert Guillem Balague, a close friend of Guardiola's.

4 Guardiola turned Man City into a trophy-winning machine with the Champions League and several Premier League titles arriving Credit: Getty

Guardiola posted on Instagram last week in support of Man City and suggested that he'll be there to help the club after they were found guilty of all serious financial breaches.

He said: "I want every single Manchester City fan across the world to know I am here; more than ever.

"I am, always have been, always will be, behind my club, my owner, my chairman, Ferran (Soriano), the players, staff, Enzo (Maresca) and you, our unique supporters.

"Let me be clear: we will get through this together. I love you all."

And Balague now believes that the former Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss will be in attendance against PSG in the Champions League, live on talkSPORT next Wednesday.

When asked about this on White and Jordan by Jim White, Balague said: "He's a bit bored. When he put the Instagram post out, it was himself. He felt he had to say this to the fans.

"I've got the impression that he would like to be there at the first game at the Etihad.

"When he puts this post out, he is backing his friends because they put everything in place for him to arrive and be successful.

"And I think he feels that he needs to back them up, and the first game at the Etihad is PSG in the Champions League."

Simon Jordan then put forward his view, as he said: "I think this is admirable of Pep Guardiola because a lot of people are cowards and they run because they don't want the association.

4 Guardiola made an emotional goodbye to City at the end of last season Credit: Getty

4 Man City have submitted an appeal and continue to insist their innocence against all charges Credit: Getty

"So for him to stick his head above the parapet, some would say is foolish and some would say he is a man of integrity and believes the relationship she has with them is meaningful, and he is going to stand by the people he believes, and there is something to be said for that."

Did Guardiola know anything?

Since the independent commission found Man City to be guilty of inflating sponsorship by around £900million, there have been a few articles suggesting that Guardiola's legacy is tainted.

Of course, Man City have submitted an appeal and are adamant that the money they received came from the UAE government and not the owner.

But on the suggestion about Guardiola, Balague said: "So, we are at this point with City that everyone goes to the fire, and it's black and white.

"Guardiola asked Mubarak Al Khadoon, two lawyers and Ferran Soriano, and he always got the same answer that everything was okay.

"Does he have to investigate? I don't know. But he is surrounded by friends who brought him over and did a lot to do so without City being where they were, they might not have convinced Pep Guardiola.

4 The time City stand accused of cheating covers two years of Guardiola's time in the blue half of Manchester Credit: Getty

"In the ten years he was in charge, the net spend was the fourth in the Premier League, and for wages, they were either first, second or third, but the gap when they were first wasn't that big.

"So they more or less played with the same money, so to me, Pep is like a jeweller who has been given stones, and he's made them into diamonds.

"I don't think he had more than two world-class players when he first arrived. [Kevin] De Bruyne wasn't."

Jordan then made the point that Guardiola was only at the Etihad for two of the years they stand being accused of cheating financially, so the majority of the 'sham' sponsorships had already been arranged.

And Balague added: "Without that growth, you don't get Guardiola, but that isn't his fault."

What happens next?

Man City's appeal has now been lodged, with the process expected to take 12 weeks.

From there, the panel have 30 days to release a verdict.

Man City will hope that the most serious charges are overturned, leading to a reduced or possibly no punishment.

But should they fail, there will be a hearing with another independent commission who will decide the punishment.

This could range from a fine to a transfer ban, and to the other end of the spectrum, there are threats of points deductions, expulsion from the league and being stripped of titles.

Sports.title: Man City warned incoming star could be snatched by Premier League rivals amid guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Cavan Sullivan may be joining Manchester City in 2027 - but he could end up at one of their rivals.

That's the view of ex-Premier League goalkeeper Brad Friedel, who has commented on the 17-year-old's future in wake of the Citizens' guilty verdict.



5 Philadelhia Union starlet Sullivan is the youngest player to feature in MLS - doing so at just 14 in 2024 Credit: Getty

The Etihad outfit were last week found guilty on each of their Premier League breach charges.

It remains to be seen what punishment will be dished out to them, which could range from points deduction to relegation and having their titles stripped.

This could potentially be bad news for USA starlet Sullivan, who is due to link up at City next year after he turns 18 in September 2027.



Should City be unable to register new players, this would leave the American's future up in the air.

Who is Cavan Sullivan?

One of the world's most talented prospects, the versatile winger made his Philadelphia Union debut in the MLS aged just 14 in 2024.



City subsequently agreed a pre-agreement deal for the player, with the mercurial talent continuing to go from strength to strength.

Featuring in 30 games across all competitions in the 2026 season for Philadelphia so far, Sullivan has chipped in with ten goals and nine assists.



His dazzling displays earned him a first call-up to USA's national team by boss Mauricio Pochettino in September, where he has since been capped on three occasions.

And on his third cap, he created history to become the Stars and Stripes' youngest ever goalscorer.

City fans have been keeping a close eye on Sullivan's development, but Friedel, who featured 82 times for the USMNT between 1992-2004, has been left unsure whether he will indeed pull on the famous sky blue jersey.

5 Sullivan scored in USA's 3-0 win over Mexico to become the youngest scorer for the national team Credit: Getty



5 The teenager is due to link up at City next year once he turns 18 Credit: Getty

Speaking to talkSPORT.com about the teenager, Friedel claimed the youngster has all the talent to become a global star, before his attention turned to City.

Could Cavan Sullivan join another team?

The ex-Aston Villa, Liverpool and Tottenham man said: "One of the things that you don't know with American players is what their mentality is going to be like when they do go to Europe.

"Sullivan seems like one that has all the right attributes, fortunately for him, he signed a contract to get out of the US when he's 18 and go over to Europe.



"The problem with that now is it's with Manchester City, so we don't really know what's going to happen there.

"But let's just say the worst happens to Man City, I'm sure somebody else will gladly take him, because he is a good talent.

"He's been playing as a winger, but he's more of a winger who likes to come inside, I do think he has qualities to be a number ten as well - he has a real chance at success."

5 It remains to be seen what punishment City will he handed following their guilty verdict Credit: Getty



Having alluded to the uncertainty surrounding City, Friedel was then asked which clubs should sign the player if Enzo Maresca's side are banned from registering new players.

And in news that City fans won't like to hear, Friedel believes his future could lie at one of their potential title rivals.

To which he remarked: "Well, if he went to Man City in the first place at 18 years of age, my assumption is he would go out on loan anyways.

"I know there are people that will think, 'No, he's going to go to Man City and start right away.'



"Well, maybe, but the probability is no, with his potential talent of being a real star, I could see another big club taking on the opportunity of signing him.

"I could see a top six or seven club in the Premier League taking him.

5 Sullivan has seven MLS goals from 24 outings in the 2026 campaign so far Credit: Getty

"But I do think that then he would need to go on loan to really learn a lot more aspects about life as a top professional player when the spotlight's on you.



"Because again, in MLS, you don't have the pressure that you have over there.

"If he were to, just to give a scenario, if he were to start four games on the bounce for a top six Premier League team, has no goals, no assists, no forward passes, no final third entries, wins no duels, etc, everyone will be on him unlike he's ever seen before.

"Whereas right now, he's just praise, praise, praise, praise, praise."

Sports.title: The truth about 'Britain's Most Insufferable YouTuber': Behind the 'rage bait', Saudi propaganda and cringe-inducing content, this is why Thogden is not living the luxury life his videos suggest
Sports.content:
‘Britain’s Most Insufferable YouTuber’ pops off the screen at you first. Next up in the search results are ‘The Thogden Files Got Worse’, ‘The Problem With Thogden’ and finally: ‘The Decay of Britain's Most Insufferable YouTuber.'

Those five seconds of scrolling tell all about the public perception of a content creator who has long ‘rage-baited’ and infuriated football fans across the internet through his match-going vlogs and streams. Disliked or not, though, this is the style that grew ‘Thogden’ into the internet phenomenon he is today.

​Born in Harrogate, Theo Ogden began his YouTube channel in 2014 while in secondary school, and has racked up a massive 2.7million subscribers and 1.6billion video views over the last 12 years. In recent years, his relentless social media output has spread to short-form content, posting to more than 700,000 followers on both TikTok and Instagram, and 150,000 more on X.

​So why does someone who – based on the numbers – seems like a popular figure, receive so much vitriol on social media?

​Mostly, the annoyance comes through the perceived irritating and cringeworthy nature of Thogden’s videos, particularly short-form content. He is a product of Mr Beast’s ever-growing cultural impact on the industry, with his overdramatic presentation style clearly catered to a younger audience.

The bizarre, childish challenges at matches, such as when he went to an Atletico Madrid match to talk in what he called ‘Naija’, (it was actually Nigerian Pidgin), until Ademola Lookman, who plays for Nigeria at international level, scored a goal. The former Fulham and Everton winger did not score. This modern approach is cringe-inducing, and in the Lookman case almost offensive, but it laps up the views.

Born in Harrogate, Theo 'Thogden' Ogden began his YouTube channel in 2014 while in secondary school, and has racked up 2.7million subscribers and 1.6billion video views

Thogden made his name live-blogging from the stands at England games, offering a new perspective that has been mimicked by countless copycats

His cringe-inducing formats strike a chord with the internet generation - such as speaking 'Naija' throughout an Atletico Madrid match in tribute to Nigeria winger Ademola Lookman

​The Bolton Wanderers fan, who grew up in Greater Manchester before moving to West Hampstead, north London in his late teens, first went viral during the 2018 World Cup in Russia - where his mother is from - as he followed Gareth Southgate’s England all the way to the heartbreaking semi-final defeat by Croatia.

​However, it was Euro 2020 where the then 20-year-old’s popularity took off. The Three Lions fanatic gave supporters a different perspective of matches, vlogging from the stands in a style that has given rise to a thousand copycats. He continued this style into club football at various teams - including his beloved Bolton - and grew his following further and further.

​But with this sort of exposure came a new level of scrutiny from doomscrollers. His comment sections were soon rife with invective language from supporters who didn’t enjoy his ‘main character syndrome’ and criticised the number of games he was able to get to at the expense of diehard fans.

​Speaking on The Fellas podcast in 2023, Thogden said: ‘If I go to a Leeds game, and I show people how good the Leeds atmosphere is, I’m showing hundreds of thousands of people who don’t know from inside the stadium. So, I’m doing a lot for them. And in return, they are constantly saying, “Oh, why’s he there? Why does he have a ticket?”

​‘Well you’re allowing loads of new people to potentially become a Leeds fan from abroad, from wherever. I don’t think people look at the full picture.’

But the full picture of his YouTube feed also shows why he’s become so polarising.

​During the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, which was shrouded in controversy surrounding human rights issues, Thogden attended all 64 matches at the tournament alongside his father Stephen Ogden, better known in his regular appearances on YouTube as ‘Thogdad’.

​The pair partnered with Crypto.com for the project, a firm that has a partnership with Donald Trump’s social media company ‘Truth Social’.

Thogden attended all 64 matches at the 2022 World Cup alongside his father Stephen Ogden, better known in his regular appearances on YouTube as ‘Thogdad’

His comment sections were soon rife with invective language from supporters who criticised the number of games he was able to get to at the expense of diehard fans

Then there was ​Thogden’s partnership with the Saudi tourist board. When Newcastle lifted the Carabao Cup last year, their first domestic trophy in 70 years, he encouraged Newcastle fans to celebrate the triumph by visiting Boulevard World, an entertainment district in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

​‘Where's the after party? Saudi Arabia! Just imagine Boulevard World, full of black and white - and it's actually easy to get there,' he shamelessly proclaimed, in 'conversation' with Thogdad for a TikTok post labelled as a 'paid partnership'. 'Sun, celebrations, and probably Joelinton on a camel.'

​It was in stark contrast to a video he made with ‘Thogdad’ four years earlier, when Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) purchased a majority stake in Newcastle.

In a video titled: ‘The Truth about Newcastle United's New Owners’, he told celebrating Newcastle fans: ‘Just have a little search into Yemen (where Saudi forces have been helping the government crackdown on Houthi rebels, with the country suffering a crippling famine), find out what's going on there, and then come back and realise, that’s behind your club. Really assess, do you think that’s the right decision?’

​A perfect example of how money can change opinions.

​There is then Thogden’s love of Morocco, but that is evidently a product of the views and adoration he gets from their football fans whenever he posts about them. Why else would he proclaim, ‘I feel Moroccan’ and that he bleeds ‘red and green’ while sporting a Morocco shirt at the World Cup?

​That video almost encapsulates Thogden. He is so wrapped up in chasing clicks and going viral that he is happy to change his ways to suit his audience. Morocco fans are viewing my content? Let me suddenly claim I am one of them.

​Moreover, there is his love of being the main character, which is a trait his most avid haters use as a stick to beat him with. A podcast with Sky Sports’ Adam Smith from last year went viral for how Thogden claimed that Lionel Messi, who he met at a VIP event in Miami, would remember him and that, in reference to arguably the greatest footballer that has ever lived, ‘there would be a smile on his face’ if they did meet again.

Thogden has focused a lot of his content on Morocco, having found himself popular with their fans

With Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi

​Thogden’s content is emblematic of the direction football media is going in. He was a poster boy for Sky Sports when they entered the ‘creatorsphere’, regularly appearing on Saturday Social - the influencer-led show that replaced the iconic Soccer AM and is infinitely less enjoyable to watch.

​We are in an age where clicks drive content and whether people like it or not, Thogden gets those clicks. You could compare him to boxing and UFC influencer Jake Paul - people love to hate him, but that just bolsters his viewership, visibility, and his bank account.

​Thogden is believed to have made most of his money through brand deals, posting videos collaborating with paid partners on social media. In the past year alone, he has worked with Pepperami, Super Snacks, Polymarket - a prediction market platform - and, biggest of all, Nike.

​A financial expert within the creator industry told Daily Mail Sport that these partnerships may not be as lucrative for Thogden as you might expect, as brands such as Crypto.com and Polymarket ‘may like to offer tickets’ (freebies) to the creator in return for ‘integrated’ videos.

​However, those brands may also offer money based on a ‘pay-per-thousand-views’ basis (known as a CPM, or Cost Per Mille). ​The financial expert tells Daily Mail Sport: ‘In industries like banking and crypto, they can pay much higher CPMs. So they might pay £40 to £60 per 1,000 views. Depending on which kind of brands, you could be making anything from £15,000 to £30,000 per video.’

​Despite the opportunities on offer given his enormous social media following, Thogden has previously revealed he does not take money from companies for videos during tournaments such as the World Cup, inferring that these are gifted partnerships in which they supply travel, accommodation, and tickets.

His accounts suggest that this may be his business model. According to filings at Companies House, Thogden is the director of two companies, Thogden Ltd and Burford Browns Ltd, but they are effectively the same business.

The former was renamed to the latter in 2024 and Thogden Ltd survived a compulsory strike-off earlier this year. It was served a first gazette notice for appearing to be inactive but subsequently avoided being dissolved after confirming to the registrar that ‘its intended future activities are lawful’.

Meeting Lionel Messi in 2024. Thogden later claimed ‘there would be a smile on (Messi's) face’ if they did meet again

He was in full effect at the 2026 World Cup, posting from high-profile matches including the final

​Burford Browns Ltd, as his production company is now known, has net assets of £631,264, as of its latest accounts. Handy, for sure, but not the trappings of a man living a complete life of luxury.

There is a common misconception in this day and age that influencers and content creators are living in mansions that seem out of this world and have swimming pools filled with cash in the back garden. There are the likes of Mr Beast and Charli D’Amelio, who have made their millions and become internet celebrities from growing Gen Z audiences whose eyes are permanently glued to screens. But they are the headline acts.

The majority of creators still willingly take on gifted partnerships alongside paid brand deals, earning an honest, healthy salary alongside enviable perks – such as football matches in Thogden’s case – while enjoying a relatively down-to-earth life.

And despite the controversies, despite the wacky formats and the criticism, Thogden carries on. If we truly are seeing the ‘decay of Britain’s most insufferable YouTuber’, then it clearly still has a way to run.

Sports.title: Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman presented with THREE world records after memorable breakthrough Premier League season
Sports.content:
Arsenal wonderkid Max Dowman has become the recipient of three Guinness world records following his stunning breakthrough campaign.

Dowman, 16, achieved the three records last season as the teenage winger was gradually handed first team opportunities by Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

Last November, Dowman became the youngest player to feature in a UEFA Champions League match when he came on as a substitute against Slavia Prague.

Dowman was 15 years and 308 days old when he made his debut in the competition, which saw him break the previous record, held by Borussia Dortmund’s Youssoufa Moukoko, by 75 days.

The attacker then made Premier League history by becoming the competition's youngest scorer at 16 years and 73 days when he netted in Arsenal's 2-0 victory over Everton in March.

Dowman broke the longstanding record held by James Vaughan, who was 16 years and 271 days when he scored for Everton against Crystal Palace in 2005 – a match which Gunners boss Arteta played in for the Toffees.

Arsenal star Max Dowman has been presented with three Guinness world records following his stunning breakthrough season

Dowman last season became the Premier League's youngest goalscorer when he scored against Everton aged 16 years and 73 days

Dowman also became the youngest player to play in the Champions League and the youngest winner of the Premier League

The third record came at the end of the season, with Dowman becoming the youngest player to win the Premier League, aged 16 and 144 days.

Dowman was presented with three official Guinness World Records certificates in a presentation at Arsenal.

He was also given the new Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027 book, in which the Arsenal star features as the opening player profile in its Class of ’27.

'The youngest player on our list, Max sums up what the Class of '27 is all about', said Tom Beckerlegge, senior editor of Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027.

'To have already achieved three Guinness World Records titles before turning 17 is extraordinary, and his story captures exactly why this generation of players is so exciting.

'Football never stands still. Records are broken, new stars emerge and every season brings fresh moments of genius that light up the game.

'The Guinness World Records Football Edition 2027 celebrates all of that - from the biggest stars in world football to the young players whose stories are only just beginning.'

Lamine Yamal, Jude Bellingham, Cole Palmer, Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappe are among other players included in the Class of '27.

GUINNESS WORLD RECORDS FOOTBALL EDITION 2027 is available in stores and online from Thursday 8 October 2026, priced £12.99.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua braced for dramatic 1am start time as Cardiff Council receive proposal for historic bout - which could see Principality Stadium stay open until 3.30am!
Sports.content:
The highly-anticipated bout between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua could be set for a 1am start time at the Principality Stadium, Cardiff, in December.

That's after Cardiff Council received an application stating the ring walks are planned to start gone midnight, with proposals for the stadium to stay open until 3.30am.

According to the BBC, Millennium Stadium Plc has applied to change its premises licence to allow the fight to take place late 'on a very limited one-off occasion'.

There is also a request to play live music until 3am on the same date, with a live performance expected before the ring walks.

It is proposed that the stadium roof is closed for the duration of the event, with enhanced security in place.

Other authorities and members of the public can make an objection until November 3, and a council hearing will be held to consider them. It is understood the permission will be granted if there are no objections.

There is a proposal for the ring walks for Tyson Fury (left) vs Anthony Joshua (right) to take place at 1am

There was initially doubt over whether the fight would take place in the United Kingdom or New York City.

It is understood Eddie Hearn pushed hard for the fight to be in Cardiff, with broadcaster Netflix keen to host it later so it can be shown at a reasonable time in the States.

Fury is currently favourite to take victory in the bout, with the Gypsy King claiming he has battled back from 28st – as heavy as an adult mountain gorilla – to chisel down to the shape he's in today.

Fury's physique has fluctuated heavily down the years – in January he described himself as a 'fat, binge-drinking junk-food addict' as he returned from retirement for a fifth time – but he is not messing around on this occasion.

Each fighter will pocket £75million from the face-off. As Daily Mail Sport revealed in September, the two fighters would have been taxed around 30 per cent of their purses in America, compared to 20 per cent in the UK, with Joshua particularly unhappy about the prospect of an extra £7.5million being added to his bill.

The two-time world champion instead demanded that his contract be honoured, which stipulated a British-based fight.

Hearn initially pushed for Wembley Stadium, but the combination of a roof over the Principality Stadium and the Welsh government’s willingness to bend their late-night curfew swung the fight towards Cardiff.

Sports.title: Gianluigi Donnarumma's defiant agent insists Man City will get 'sporting justice' in appeal over guilty verdict - claiming that 'everyone is calm' after club 'reassured' the goalkeeper
Sports.content:
Man City will achieve 'sporting justice' after their appeal and everyone at the club is 'calm', according to Gianluigi Donnarumma's agent. City being found guilty of the biggest cheating scandal in British sporting history has rocked football and the Premier League since news of the verdict broke. They've lodged an appeal against the findings that they artificially inflated commercial revenues by £830million through ‘sham’ contracts with a range of Abu Dhabi-based companies. And goalkeeper Donnarumma's agent, Enzo Raiola, revealed the Italian has been given assurances by the club, who still insist on their innocence in the wake of the damning verdict by the independent commission. He told Radio Napoli Centrale, per Calciomercato: 'Can the Manchester City chaos change anything? No, it won't change anything for us or for Gigio. News comes out periodically. 'The club has spoken to Gigio, and everyone is calm. Now there are important matches against Liverpool and PSG, and then sporting justice will take its course. But Gigio has received reassurances from Manchester City.' Gianluigi Donnarumma's agent insists Man City have told him to remain calm about his future If City fail in their appeal, they will face severe sanctions which could include expulsion from the Premier League, future points deductions, stripping of titles and transfer bans. A range of those punishments would place Donnarumma and his City team-mates in a situation with extreme uncertainty surrounding their futures. City face Liverpool at Anfield in their first game back since the verdict was published and Merseyside police are prepped for an angry reception. As Daily Mail Sport's Mike Keegan reported, there are concerns the visitors' team bus could be met with a pre-planned, hostile ‘welcome’. One social media post is advertising a ‘Bus Greeting’ around two hours before the 4.30pm kick-off on Anfield Road. Fans are asked to bring ‘flags, banners, pyros, flares, kopparbergs’. A wink emoji is placed after Kopparberg, which is a popular cider served in a bottle. Police are aware of the poster and have said that they will have ‘an appropriate policing plan in place’. Next Wednesday, City will play their first game at the Etihad since they were found guilty and Pep Guardiola will be in attendance in a show of solidarity. Guardiola will be joined at the Etihad Stadium by the City board, including chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak, for the club’s first home European match since his summer departure. Guardiola leapt to City’s defence a day after the three-person independent commission’s verdict was made public and Donnarumma's agent's comments are further evidence of the club insisting on business as usual.

Sports.title: Scott McTominay returns to Napoli training for the first time since undergoing successful heart surgery in Manchester last month
Sports.content:
Scott McTominay is back in Napoli training after undergoing successful heart surgery in September.

The Scotland international, 29, has been diagnosed with 'a mild benign arrhythmia', which is an abnormal or irregular heart rhythm deemed non-serious and posing no significant risk to overall health.

Before the surgery, the British Heart Foundation explained that the procedure McTominay was having would see heat or cold energy used to create tiny scars in the heart to block faulty signals and restore a typical heartbeat.

The procedure took place at the start of September in Manchester, and was initially supposed to be on the sidelines for two weeks before returning to training.

But he was ruled out of Scotland action during the international break and is now back on the grass with Napoli and in contention to line up against Frosinone on Saturday.

McTominay's fiancee sent a touching message to her partner after the news of the surgery was made public.

Scott McTominay has returned to Napoli training after undergoing successful heart surgery

His fiancee, Cam Reading (right), sent him a heartwarming message prior to the surgery

Accompanied by two heart emojis, Cam Reading wrote: 'By your side, always so proud of you.'

The couple have been together since around 2022, and became engaged soon after.

McTominay also spoke about his impending surgery, and insisted the issue is nothing to worry about.

'I'm fine,' he told reporters. 'The procedure was something I'd planned to do with the club for quite a while.'

McTominay has been a revelation since joining the Italian side from Manchester United in 2024.

The Scottish star has scored 27 goals and added ten assists in just 82 appearances, while he played a key role in their Serie A triumph in 2024-25.

Under Antonio Conte, he evolved from a dependable squad player at Old Trafford into one of Europe's most effective box-crashing midfielders, scoring 12 Serie A goals and earning the division's MVP award during that superb campaign.

He also came 18th in the Ballon d'Or rankings in 2025, ahead of players including Jude Bellingham, Erling Haaland and Michael Olise.

McTominay repeatedly delivered in big moments, none more so than on the final day of the season when an acrobatic strike put Napoli ahead as they clinched the title over Inter Milan.

His impact prompted comparisons with Napoli icon Diego Maradona, with the Argentine's son even likening the Scot to Jesus.

Sports.title: Should McBurnie be dropped? Who can step in for toiling Gunn? And is the new system working? The big decisions facing Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli
Sports.content:
Widely regarded as a bold and refreshing appointment by the Scottish Football Association after the Steve Clarke era ground to a halt, Sebastien Pocognoli became Scotland manager with a reputation for playing entertaining front-foot football which could still deliver results.

While there’s been wide acknowledgement that the Belgian is going to need time for his ideas to take root and manifest themselves in positive results, four points from four Nations League games represents slow progress.

If Saturday’s win in Skopje felt like a step forward, then the manner of the defeat to Slovenia at Hampden was a reality check.

Pocognoli’s players now need an extraordinary turn of events to finish second in their section and become a pot two team in the Euro 2028 draw in December.

Sebastien Pocognoli has some big issues to ponder ahead of the next Scotland match

Of greater concern in the long run, though, was how unconvincing the side were across the elongated international break.

With just a month to go before the campaign concludes with a home game with North Macedonia and a trip to Switzerland, Daily Mail Sport looks at the key issues which the manager must ponder.

Tear up the system or double down on it?

At both Union SG and Monaco, Pocognoli fielded three-at-the-back so no one should be in any way surprised that that is how his Scotland side are set up.

Is he trying to shoe-horn players into a 3-4-2-1 when a 4-4-2 or a 4-3-3 might better suit their talents? It would appear so.

Ben Gannon-Doak, the squad’s most explosive player, is a winger by trade. Try as he might, he doesn’t really have the skill set for the defensive side of the game.

Oli McBurnie is a striker who needs someone alongside him. Little wonder his goal drought in Dark Blue has now extended to 20 matches.

As compelling as the argument is for the Belgian to change tack and put more square pegs in square holes by reverting to the back-four that was briefly witnessed late in Tuesday’s match, that’s just not going to happen.

Tony Docherty travelled to La Manga so he could get up to speed on Pocognoli’s blueprint to ensure players moving up from his under-21 side are already prepared for the demands. So, ripping it up and starting again just doesn’t appear to be an option.

Can it be tweaked?

Absolutely. And it can also be better executed.

Essentially, the plan is for the defence to play a high line, thus cutting down the distances between them and the midfield and the front line. This is designed to limit the space in which the opponents can win possession and play. The high press also designed to shut them off at source and prevent players from simply knocking the ball over the top into the vacant space.

Pocognoli’s main gripe after Tuesday was that his players didn’t get their distances right, meaning they were not compact and their press was rendered ineffective. Slovenia played through them too easily. He also picked up on the defence’s tendency to drop deep – contradicting the game plan. For the system to work, the players must be braver and more aggressive in its execution.

Scotland were better when Billy Gilmour stepped forward to essentially become a third No10 in a 3-3-3-1. All too briefly, Slovenia struggled to get out. We can expect more of this.

Kieron Bowie, who surprisingly started on the bench, looks comfortable playing the lone striker role. McBurnie would benefit from having someone beside him, perhaps in a 3-4-1-2. One possible way to get Gannon-Doak into the team without exposing his defensive limitations would be playing him centrally.

Angus Gunn has struggled for form in Scotland's Nations League campaign

Are the gloves off?

For so long, Scotland managers were spoiled for choice when it came to goalkeepers. It’s now the problem position.

Three keepers travelled to the World Cup. Craig Gordon has since retired while Liam Kelly doesn’t get a regular game for Rangers.

Angus Gunn featured in the three games in the US despite playing just once for Nottingham Forest last season.

Now a regular in the MLS with San Jose – he’s made 11 appearances this term – the hope was that he’d arrive for Pocognoli’s first camp razor sharp.

Alas, that’s been wishful thinking. Gunn could have done better with two of Switzerland’s goals last week and should have prevented Aljosa Matko from netting Slovenia’s first.

But aside from his questionable shot-stopping, Gunn is not the best with the ball at his feet.

In terms of the current options available, that accolade belongs to Scott Bain – a keeper who can hold his own playing outfield at training. The difficulty is, of course, that his form with Falkirk has shaded from last season.

It feels like a question of Pocognoli keeping a watching brief on this before naming his squad for North Macedonia and Switzerland. There’s a lot to be said for just playing the man on form.

Is it time to draw a line under McBurnie in a Scotland jersey?

As the 13th minute came and went on Tuesday, the Hull forward chalked up an unwanted milestone. That of playing 1000 minutes in Dark Blue and not finding the back of the net.

You’d have needed a heart of stone not to feel for the player as his 20th cap proved to be another episode filled with frustration.

The less said the better about his attempt to fire into an unguarded net on 31 minutes. Fortunately, Ryan Christie then backheeled the loose ball home.

Hull City striker Oli McBurnie has now failed to score in 20 Scotland appearances

You absolutely cannot fault McBurnie’s desire to succeed with Scotland. In La Manga, he spoke with pride about being recalled by Pocognoli and with humility about why Steve Clarke had overlooked him for so long.

But you cannot ignore the evidence of your own eyes. The 19 goals he hit in Hull’s promotion campaign have not yet translated into a one at the start of the Pocognoli era.

With Che Adams likely to be available for the next double header and with Bowie having scored and caught the eye, McBurnie’s spot in the squad looks vulnerable.

How does Scott McTominay fit in?

Having undergone a procedure for a mild, benign arrhythmia on September 8, he has now resumed individual training with Napoli and is awaiting final medical checks to regain the necessary clearance to resume playing.

With his first-team return imminent – possibly as soon as this weekend against Frosinone – the midfielder should be available for Pocognoli’s next camp.

The days of him being used as a centre-half are – hopefully – over, it’s a matter of where the Belgian slots him in and who he displaces. Deployed by his club as either a No8 or a No10, it seems unlikely that he’ll tread on the toes of Lewis Ferguson or his club-mate Gilmour, who tend to play deeper.

The smart money would be on the manager perming any two from the three of McTominay, John McGinn and Ryan Christie and using them as the support to the forward.
