Sports.title: Lionel Messi officially waves farewell to Argentina with emotional statement and admits his final send-off brought 'joys and sorrows' - prompting reply from long-time rival Cristiano Ronaldo
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi officially waves farewell to Argentina with emotional statement and admits his final send-off brought 'joys and sorrows' - prompting reply from long-time rival Cristiano Ronaldo

Lionel Messi's emotional farewell message to Argentina fans inspired a reply from an unlikely source – Cristiano Ronaldo.

Having scored in his final outing in front of 85,000 supporters for his goodbye game on Tuesday night at Estadio Monumental, Messi cut an emotional figure on the pitch and has now reflected on the 'joys and sorrows' of his international career.

Ronaldo, who posted a very different kind of statement explaining his explosive Portugal walkout just a day earlier, was among those to offer some kind words in reply to his old foe.

The 41-year-old wrote: 'Leo, so many years defending your country and a history that will last forever. All my respect for what you have achieved with Argentina. A hug.'

Messi, 39, who inspired Argentina to their World Cup triumph four years ago, had been overwhelmed by the reception he was given on Tuesday in Buenos Aires.

His statement read: 'Yesterday was my last game and I already miss wearing blue and white. I know I'm making the right decision. It was an incredible road, filled with joys and also some sorrows, but I'm clear that it was worth every step I took.

Lionel Messi shared his parting message and a number of photos after the farewell game

Cristiano Ronaldo posted a kind message to his old rival, who hung up his international boots

'And I'm left with a lot to say. It is impossible for me to express everything I feel in a few words or in a post. This trip would have been impossible without my family, who always stood by my side and supported me, especially during the difficult times, when I needed it most.

'They were also indispensable my friends, all the colleagues and technicians I had, along with their technical bodies.

'I don't want to forget Diego, who put our country where it deserved to be and who, as I always say, I know that he helped us being here with us and also from heaven, in every step we took.

'Thanks to the clubs I played in, for always respecting my feelings and allowing me to dedicate myself to my country when it was time to put on the national team shirt. And, of course, thank God: without His guidance and His will, we wouldn't even be dreaming of having come this far.

'I am a grateful person. I love you so much, I will miss you and I will always thank you for being by our side, by my side.'

Messi netted a penalty against Benin, taking his final tally of Argentina goals to 126 in 208 appearances. He also delivered 62 assists and has won more World Cup games (23) than any player in history.

He won six trophies on the international stage at all age levels and retires from international duty regarded as the greatest player of his generation.

Messi and Ronaldo are pictured together at the 2019 Champions League draw

Cristiano Ronaldo (left) accused Jorge Jesus (right) of breaking promises and outlined exactly why he walked out on Portugal in a 2000-word statement

While Messi is being garlanded with praise for his achievements, his old rival Ronaldo is embroiled in a row that has threatened to tarnish his own legacy with the national team.

Ronaldo published a 2000-word statement eviscerating manager Jorge Jesus for 'broken promises', apologising to his team-mates and Portugal fans for walking out on the team and even comparing himself to Pele.

Ronaldo also posted the extraordinary eight points of apology he says he agreed Jesus would give publicly.

Ronaldo rounded off his statement by declaring himself available after any suspension is dished out to him, calling it the 'purest of truths'.

'If I am physically well, playing for my club, with goals I hope, after serving the suspension that may be applied to me, I will be available, as I have always been until today, to compete and win for our national team,' he pledged.

Whether it is possible for Jesus and Ronaldo to reconcile remains to be seen but with his 42nd birthday approaching in February, the explosive row could well be the end of the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's future in competitive international football.

THE EIGHT-POINT APOLOGY RONALDO WANTED 1. I myself, and no one else, proposed to Cristiano a plan for him this sporting season with the National Team. It was a long and very good conversation. 2. I know how much he lives and loves the national team and the weight he has in the world, and even more the weight and the positive influence he has had on the national team for 24 consecutive years. 3. The plan I proposed to Cristiano was accepted. 4. He never questioned my options. He was exemplary, loyal and professional. 5. The match in Norway was not part of the plan I drew up for him. However, I felt that he had managed to recover physically from the first match and I warned him that I might have to use him. Cristiano agreed. 6. I made a mistake by putting someone of the stature of Pelé or Maradona on to warm up and then not putting him in the game. If it were today I would not do it. 7. To close the subject: I want Cristiano in the National Team. In fact I do not want him a little, I want him a lot. Fortunately he also believes in me. He believed at Al Nassr and he does here as well. 8. About not greeting the fans. We have already spoken about that. Someone who has played more than 230 matches for the national team does not receive lessons from me on love for Portugal. It was a moment of frustration that erases nothing. He is the player who gives the most autographs, takes the most selfies, and shows the most affection to the fans. Let us not invent problems where they do not exist. When we are not happy we react.

When asked about Ronaldo's statement attacking him, Jesus replied curtly: 'I read the statement, and now, as I do every day, I'm going to the federation to work, to think about the team and the national team.’

In spite of Ronaldo's own self-inflicted circumstances, the message to his old foe is to his credit and the years they spent vying for the Ballon d'Or and competing with each other as talismanic presences for Real Madrid and Barcelona shaped the rivalry for years.

Ronaldo is still desperate to reach 1000 career goals and wants to net the landmark figure in the colours of his country. Whether he'll be reintegrated after his latest damaging behaviour remains to be seen.

Sports.title: The Coldplay Kiss-Cam meets football! Female fan separates herself from 'boyfriend' in excruciating moment when cameras turned to them at Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell
Sports.content:
A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell.

The couple were among over 80,000 spectators present at the Estadio Monumental as Argentina paid tribute to the legendary star in a friendly against Benin.

Cameras picked out the couple during the pre-match build-up, with footage shared on social media showing the female fan realising they were being shown on the big screens.

The fan was then seen awkwardly removing her boyfriend's hand from her shoulder.

She then began adjusting her hair while glancing in his direction and exchanging words.

Football fans were quick to begin speculating about the moment on social media, with some joking it was 'Argentina's Coldplay moment'.

A female football fan was seen separating herself from her boyfriend after the couple were caught on camera during Lionel Messi's Argentina farewell

Fans joked on social media that it was Argentina's 'Coldplay moment', referencing the infamous kiss-cam which caught a a CEO and his co-worker embracing last year

Others gave a more sympathetic view of the clip, suggesting the female fan had merely wanted to adjust their hair

The comments referenced the infamous kiss-cam at a Coldplay gig last year that caught a CEO and his co-worker embracing.

'Coldplay Kiss Cam moment at Lionel Messi farewell,' one fan joked.

'It feels like she deliberately put some distance between herself and the camera once she noticed it,' another wrote.

'I feel that pain bro,' a third added.

Others, however, offered a more sympathetic view of the clip with one fan saying: 'Am I being naive to theorize that she might have just wanted his arm off her so she could fix her hair?'

The match itself proved an emotional occasion as Messi said farewell to Argentina's national team.

The 39-year-old capped his 208th and final appearance for his country with a goal and two assists as Argentina waved goodbye to its hero with a 3-0 win.

Following the game, tributes to Messi continued with an emotional musical performance before Messi took the microphone himself.

Lionel Messi played his final match for Argentina in an emotional affair in Buenos Aires

Fireworks were launched into the night sky above the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires

At the national anthem, Messi's sons - Thiago, Mateo and Ciro - joined their father

Messi scored his final goal for Argentina from the penalty spot as they earned a 3-0 win over Benin

'My dad is the first person I think about tonight,' he began, remembering his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 back in August.

'I can only thank you all. It has been a huge pride to defend this shirt for over 20 years. We never stopped fighting, never stopped giving everything. Playing for Argentina is the most beautiful thing.'

Messi's speech left supporters and players such as Enzo Fernandez struggling to contain their emotions.

'I want to thank all of my teammates. You made all of my dreams come true... I was surrounded by warriors. I'm going to miss this,' he continued.

'This may be the saddest day of my career, leaving the national team. I don't want to leave this place. I don't want to leave the field... I love all of you, and I will miss all of you. I am proud to be Argentinian.'

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel’s four demands including eye-watering wage and snubbed Man Utd request
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel’s four demands including eye-watering wage and snubbed Man Utd request

JJ Gabriel's camp reportedly several demands as Manchester United looked to keep the academy star

View 3 Images Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel requested to leave the club last month (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel's representatives made a series of demands to Manchester United before requesting the teenager's exit from Old Trafford last month. The academy prodigy recently turned 16 and could be on his way out of the club after asking for his registration to be cancelled.

‌



‌



While the Red Devils rejected the request, Gabriel could still secure a move abroad if he holds a European passport through either parent. United appeared to have already mapped out a clear route to the first team for the gifted youngster, who had been on course to become the club's youngest-ever player.

‌



The Manchester Evening News reported that United had previously gone to considerable lengths to retain Gabriel's services, including arranging a meeting with then-first team boss Ruben Amorim and an introduction to Sir Alex Ferguson. The club told Gabriel he could become the future face of the club and he was regularly involved in training under Michael Carrick, featuring for the senior side during pre-season.

‌



A full debut had seemed a matter of when rather than if, before Gabriel's camp submitted the request to leave. The youngster has since been linked with leading European clubs, though no official move has yet materialised. Here is a round-up of the demands that Gabriel's team reportedly made in recent weeks.

Having already turned 15 before this year's cut-off date, Gabriel is eligible to feature in the Premier League this season. He could also have appeared for Carrick's side in both the Carabao Cup and Champions League, but was omitted from the club's A list in the latter competition, ruling him out of the victory over Sabah.

‌



ESPN reports that United had accepted Gabriel's request to be handed the No. 77 squad number this season. The Red Devils also petitioned the Premier League to permit the 16-year-old to wear 'Gabriel JR' on the back of his shirt on his behalf.

After scooping the U18 Premier League Player of the Season award last term, Gabriel began the new campaign by continuing to progress through the club's academy ranks. While awaiting his senior bow, the attacking midfielder notched two goals and two assists across two U21 outings and also bagged a hat-trick for the U19s against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League.

View 3 Images Gabriel has been involved in first team training under Michael Carrick (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

First team training

Gabriel notably featured during pre-season and was handed an unofficial debut in a friendly against Atletico Madrid. However, his camp reportedly made it clear that a place in first-team training was expected.

Sky Sports reports that Gabriel was instructed by his family not to return to Carrington alongside the club's other U21 players at the start of pre-season. The first team squad were due back a week later and returning at the same time as other academy players was viewed as unacceptable for the teenage prodigy.

‌



Game time plan

The Manchester Evening News reported that Gabriel's representatives believed the emerging talent should feature for at least 20 minutes across United's fixtures against Sabah, Brighton and Bournemouth, a request which was snubbed. Gabriel was unable to take part against Sabah in the Champions League after being left out of the A squad, but had been tipped to appear against Brighton in the Carabao Cup. Meanwhile, United are due to meet Bournemouth in the Premier League on October 25.

View 3 Images Gabriel scored 26 goals in 29 games for Manchester United U18s last term (Image: Alex Livesey/Getty Images)

It is claimed that Gabriel's camp had pinpointed the three fixtures and wanted the 16-year-old to be handed playing time before entering discussions over a scholarship agreement. He would still have become the club's youngest-ever player in the Brighton cup clash but the request to terminate his registration was submitted ahead of the match, resulting in Gabriel being omitted from the matchday squad.

Article continues below

Salary demands

Gabriel could have signed a pre-contract with United upon turning 16, with professional contracts permitted after a player's 17th birthday. However, Bayern Munich are among several clubs, including Real Madrid and Barcelona, to be linked with the teenager after his request to leave Old Trafford.

The Times reports that the German outfit are keen on Gabriel but unwilling to satisfy the seven-figure wage demands. As United have declined to terminate Gabriel's contract, he is prevented from joining another English club until next summer but could choose to move overseas if he possesses a European passport.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Champions League concern raised as Pep Guardiola return confirmed
Sports.content:
Man City have lodged their appeal against an independent commission finding them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog on Thursday, October 8, where we will bring you the latest after an independent commission found Manchester City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly worded report released last week.

City have been accused of breaking financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18. An independent commission concluded that more than £830million of owner funding was used to inflate revenues and enable the club to comply with Premier League and UEFA regulations through a series of 'sham' arrangements.

The Etihad club, though, are adamant they have done nothing wrong, insisting they are innocent and that they have a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence to support their position as they lodged their appeal last week. However, senior figures within English football are now reportedly concerned that City could play in the Champions League next season even if they are relegated from the Premier League this season.

While in a show of support to his old club, Pep Guardiola will be back at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday night to watch his old side take on Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. But former Match of the Day host Gary Lineker believes City should 'own' their behaviour and warned they should expect to lose their titles. There is still much discussion about potential outcomes, so stay right here for all of the latest...

Sports.title: Sir Alex Ferguson sheds light on secret Pep Guardiola dinner as he admits Man Utd regret
Sports.content:
Sir Alex Ferguson sheds light on secret Pep Guardiola dinner as he admits Man Utd regret

Sir Alex Ferguson has opened up about a dinner he had with Pep Guardiola one year before he selected his Manchester United successor

View 3 Images Sir Alex Ferguson met with Pep Guardiola just eight months before his Manchester United exit (Image: Getty)

Sir Alex Ferguson wishes a 2012 dinner with Pep Guardiola had taken place earlier so he could have convinced the Spaniard to replace him at Manchester United. Guardiola had already committed his future to Bayern Munich and went on to manage rivals Manchester City.

‌



‌



It has been 13 years since Ferguson left United. In his nearly 27-year tenure, the Scot cemented his status as an Old Trafford immortal, winning 13 Premier League titles, two Champions League crowns and a haul of domestic and international honours.

‌



David Moyes was handpicked to follow in his footsteps but infamously found those boots too grand to fill. He lasted just 10 months in the job after being hired in July 2013 and was out the door by April 2014.

‌



Reflecting in his new book, Games of My Life, Ferguson recalls a meeting he had with Guardiola a year before he called it quits. The Spanish boss had impressed as Barcelona manager and had all but signed with Bayern. But Ferguson says if he could turn back the clock, he'd have staged the dinner earlier and tried to coax him to United.

Antonio Conte drops huge Man Utd hint as pressure ramps up on Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Cristiano Ronaldo's wife deletes fake Sir Alex Ferguson quote after dig at Portugal boss READ MORE :

Guardiola won a continental sextuple in 2009 as Barcelona boss and after joining Bayern in 2013, he won seven major trophies. His time at City - which has been called into question following the club's guilty financial charges ruling, which they have appealed and continue to deny - was littered with success.

View 3 Images Guardiola went on to triumph with United's city rivals (Image: Getty)

‌



He won six top-flight titles and the Champions League, among many other pieces of silverware in England. But things could have been different. Ferguson penned: "Over the past ten years, I have often wondered what might have happened if the dinner I had with Pep in New York in 2012 had taken place a couple of months earlier.

"At the time, I hadn't decided for certain that I was going to retire. And Pep was convinced that, after achieving huge success in just four years in La Liga with a Continental treble as well as a League and Champions League double, he wanted to try life in the Bundesliga with Bayern Munich.

"If I could rewind time, we would have dined some months earlier, I would have poured plenty of Tignanello (Italian wine) and I would have tried my hardest to convince him that his future lay in Manchester. Unfortunately for us, it did. Enough said."

‌



Ferguson had not yet decided to retire when he met with Guardiola, but after the death of his late wife Cathy's sister in December 2012, he made the difficult decision to depart Old Trafford.

Ferguson continued: "Pep has set a breathtaking standard for the current generation of players or anybody aspiring to become a manager. Draped in Barcelona's blue and garnet from the time he was born, he had a brilliant club career and was one of the best creative midfielders in the game during the 1990s.

View 3 Images Ferguson details the meeting in his new book (Image: Sean Pollock)

‌



"During his playing days, Pep had more than a taste of success - he positively feasted on it. He also had the opportunity to play for a series of strong personalities with different approaches to managing - Johan Cruyff, Bobby Robson and Louis van Gaal.

"Pep became manager of Barcelona when he was just thirty-seven years old. When I see some of the game's biggest stars leave the field and immediately take a manager's job without much preparation or experience, my heart sinks. It often ends badly, especially for the Premier League players.

"The stakes are too high. You're right in everyone's crosshairs. The public expect that your success on the field will automatically transfer to the dugout. Former players are impatient to make the transition to the top tier. Pep Guardiola is the most celebrated example of a manager who started with a top club when he was relatively young."

Article continues below

Games of My Life by Alex Ferguson publishes on 8th October by Macmillan.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Record-breaking bid made for wonderkid as race for 'unsellable' star heats up
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Record-breaking bid made for wonderkid as race for 'unsellable' star heats up

Liverpool are preparing for their Premier League return against Manchester City but there's no shortage of transfer news around Anfield

View 2 Images Mexico prodigy Gilberto Mora has reportedly been subject of a reord-breaking Liverpool bid (Image: 2026 MB Media)

Liverpool return to action following an extended international break hoping to pick up where they left off three weeks ago. The Reds won back-to-back games before the pause in play and face an immediate test of their credentials at home to Manchester City on Sunday.

‌



‌



Andoni Iraola's side are back up to sixth in the table following an underwhelming start to the campaign. However, that focus on this season's prospects hasn't limited the number of transfer links making their way through the rumour mill.

‌



Speculation suggests the Reds have at least one major move lining up in time for the winter transfer window. Mirror Football breaks down all the latest stories coming out of Anfield ahead of this weekend's comeback.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Record-breaking Mora bid

TUDN has reported Liverpool have registered a record-breaking bid for Mexico wonderkid Gilberto Mora. The 17-year-old has been linked with Arsenal, Barcelona and Real Madrid since breaking onto the scene at Tijuana in 2024.

Mora became the youngest player to represent Mexico at a World Cup when he featured for El Tri this summer. And interest in his signature is escalating as he prepares to turn 18 next week.

‌



According to TUDN, Liverpool's offer is worth 'in excess of £38million', which would make him Liga MX's biggest export of all time. The attacking midfielder, who can also play on the left wing, looks set to become one of the hottest commodities on the market next year.

The former Paris Saint-Germain and Benfica playmaker has risen to become a key staple in Florence and is still just 22. After being linked with a number of midfielders over the summer, Liverpool may have need of reinforcements in the middle of the park next year.

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: JJ Gabriel gets reality check as wanted star puts contract talks on hold

Manchester United have had distractions during the extended international break but are now ready to return to Premier League action

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel's future remains up in the air (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

After a three-week break, Manchester United are closing in on a return to Premier League action. Their international stars will return as Michael Carrick prepares to welcome Roberto De Zerbi and Tottenham to Old Trafford.

‌



‌



There has been plenty in the way of distractions, and not just in terms of United stars' appearances for their respective national teams. Much of the off-field chat has concerned JJ Gabriel, whose future has yet to be resolved.

‌



October is a busy month on the pitch for Carrick's team. After Spurs' weekend visit there are five more matches in all competitions, including Champions League trips to Atletico Madrid and Como.

‌



We've got some more on Gabriel for you today, as well as an update on another potential target. Here are out latest lines.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Premier League injury news: Club by Club updates and potential return dates READ MORE :

Sir Alex Ferguson was one day from becoming Arsenal boss as contract offer revealed READ MORE :

Gabriel handed warning

Former Manchester United defender Phil Bardsley has warned JJ Gabriel he doesn't believe the youngster is ready for Premier League football. It comes amid suggestions a lack of first team action is behind the teenager's desire to leave the club.

‌



"From the outside, physically I don't think he's ready to be thrown in at the level yet," Bardsley told talkSPORT. "I think from years gone by, you look at players who have physically developed. You have [Wayne] Rooney, for instance, who was ready to go and play at that age.

"Look at the boy at the minute, his abilities are obviously there, he's an outstanding talent and hopefully goes on to be a great player. But I think the timing's a bit off, the way things are at the club and the way it came out.

"But I believe it's been orchestrated by agents, parents, and pushing for these things when you're at such a delicate age and you're in a transition into men's football. I think you need to be patient."

‌



Kofane contract talks stall

View 2 Images Christian Kofane has yet to agree new terms with Bayer Leverkusen (Image: AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

Manchester United and Arsenal have been handed a boost with the news that Christian Kofane has reportedly put contract talks on hold. The Bayer Leverkusen star was linked with a Premier League move over the summer and now the two big-hitters have made contact with his representatives.

According to SportBild, this interest has been there for a while. Kofane's current Leverkusen deal runs until 2029 and has not agreed to improved terms which could keep him at the BayArena until 2031.

Article continues below

The Cameroonian is still said to be open to an extension, though the terms don't appear to align with what he wants. The Bundesliga club look to be ready to offer him a significant bump on the salary agreed when joining during Erik ten Hag's brief tenure but some things still need to be ironed out and United or their league rivals could yet take advantage.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: £21m January transfer target identified as major announcement made
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: £21m January transfer target identified as major announcement made

Arsenal are eyeing a big January deal

View 3 Images Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has extended his stay with the club (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

With the international break now officially over, Arsenal’s players can begin preparing for the resumption of Premier League football. Mikel Arteta’s side return from the three-week international break with a home fixture against Leeds United, where they’re expected to get straight back to winning ways.

‌



‌



It comes after a hugely disappointing result in their last game before the break - a 3-0 drubbing at Brighton last month. However, Arteta’s side remain second in the league, having kick-started their title defence this season with seven wins across all competitions.

‌



Several of Arsenal’s key players have been in great form for their nations over the break. Bukayo Saka, Viktor Gyokeres and Mikel Merino all got on the scoresheet more than once.

‌



However, there are also those who came away from the Nations League worse for wear, including Ezri Konsa, Kai Havertz and Christos Tzolis, who are racing to return from injury in time for Leeds. Now, Mirror Football brings you two of the latest developments involving Arsenal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Arsenal fans should savour every minute of Mikel Arteta - this could be his last contract READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta signs new Arsenal contract as he becomes highest-paid Premier League boss READ MORE :

£21m January target 'identified'

View 3 Images Arsenal have been linked with a January move for 17-year-old Gilberto Mora (Image: 2026 MB Media)

‌



Arsenal have emerged as serious contenders for the signature of 17-year-old Mexican starlet Gilberto Mora. TEAMtalk reports that the Gunners have already made contact over a potential January deal for the Club Tijuana attacking midfielder.

Mora will turn 18 this month, meaning Arsenal, who are long-term admirers, can sign him in January. He remains under contract with the Xolos until 2029, but FIFA rules that blocked an international move while he was a minor no longer apply once he turns 18.

Scouts monitored him during the World Cup, where he became Mexico’s youngest-ever player at the tournament. He has already represented his nation 13 times, leading to interest from other big clubs such as Real Madrid and Barcelona

‌



The report claims Arsenal are prepared to move more 'aggressively' than their Premier League rivals and other European sides as they look to pull off what would be a real coup. It also states that Mora has a release clause in the region of €20–25million (£16.9-£21.1m).

Major announcement made

View 3 Images Arsenal have announced Mikel Arteta's new contract (Image: Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Arsenal announced on Wednesday that Arteta has signed a mega new contract with the club. The Spaniard, who led the club to their first title in 22 years last season, has put pen to paper on a new deal which will keep him at the Emirates up to 2030.

‌



Arteta joined the club as head coach in late 2019 during a difficult period for the north Londoners. The manager is now set to be the highest-paid boss in the Premier League, following Pep Guardiola’s departure last summer.

BBC Sport reports the new contract is an increase from his current salary of £10m per year, plus an additional £5m in bonuses. It also means the 44-year-old will pass a decade in charge at the club, making him comfortably the longest-serving boss in the top flight.

Arteta said: "It's a privilege to commit my future to the club and to continue to work with exceptional people who want the best for Arsenal. This club is unique, its character and the way it makes you feel, and I have a great sense of privilege that our journey together will continue.

‌



"We have already built a special bond and created memories that will last a lifetime, and what is so exciting is that this is only the beginning of what we can achieve together. I'm extremely grateful to Stan and Josh (Kroenke) for their trust and support, and feel honoured to be leading this club through such a special period in its 140-year history.

"This is such a proud moment for me and my family. I feel the love and respect from our fantastic supporters, and they have mine – and ours - in return."

Sports.title: Gary Lineker makes Man City punishment prediction as club chiefs told to 'own it'
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker makes Man City punishment prediction as club chiefs told to 'own it'

Manchester City have been handed a new punishment verdict courtesy of Gary Lineker with a clear message also sent to the club's higher-ups

View 2 Images Gary Lineker has offered his thoughts on Manchester City's potential punishment (Image: (Photo by James Klug/Getty Images))

Gary Lineker has predicted that Manchester City could lose their Premier League titles as punishment for their rule breaches. The Premier League revealed the findings of the independent panel last Tuesday with City found guilty off all financial charges.

‌



‌



City have lodged their appeal against the decision with the outcome of that expected to arrive in January. Simultaneously, a hearing into their potential sanctions will take place with a significant points deduction to essentially relegate them from the Premier League.

‌



A hefty fine and transfer ban are also punishments that can be implemented but Gary Lineker has stated he would not be shocked if the stripping of Premier League titles is the route taken and that club chiefs should stop fighting to try and prove their innocence.

‌



Gianluigi Donnarumma's agent issues public statement on Man City guilty verdict READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

"It looks really bad for Manchester City," he said at Leaders Week London 2026 at Stamford Bridge. "When they talk about the Premier League conspiracy theories, you just think to yourself, well, this is actually the last thing in the world that the Premier League would want.

"So, I'd love to see City now just own it and just say, 'OK, we got it wrong but for the good of the game, we'll accept it, accept whatever punishment comes our way and we'll carry on.

‌



"That would be a blessing and they could save their face a little bit. At the moment that doesn't look very likely. But it is damaging. I wouldn't be surprised if it goes down the route of titles being stripped.

"Ultimately, who suffers from that? Players and fans. It's going to be one of those punishments, and it has to be, obviously, severe, because we are talking about a lot of offences.

View 2 Images Manchester City players will suffer from the 114 financial charges verdict according to Gary Lineker

‌



"So it's going to be difficult, and everyone will have a different idea of what this should be. It's not something I've really experienced very often in my career.

"I remember when English clubs were banned from Europe, and it cost me playing in the European Cup for Everton. So, again, players will suffer from this, and that's that."

City have already successfully overturned a Champions League ban imposed by UEFA and will be aiming to replicate that outcome with this ruling. Just over a week has passed since the Premier League announced the findings from the eight-week hearing that concluded in late 2024.

‌



It has subsequently emerged that City were actually made aware of the verdict over the summer and still proceeded to splash out around £400million in the transfer market. Arsenal, Liverpool, Tottenham and Manchester United, who all reserved the legal right to seek compensation, were the next parties reportedly informed of the decision, with the remaining 15 Premier League clubs notified afterwards.

City are set to take on one of those sides in Liverpool this Sunday, with an intensely hostile reception expected to greet them at Anfield.

Sports.content:
Declan Rice will match Arsenal's top earner after contract negotiation breakthrough

Declan Rice is poised to pen fresh terms at Arsenal, having established himself as one of the key players under Mikel Arteta's management following a £105million move from West Ham

View 2 Images Declan Rice will soon sign a new Arsenal contract (Image: Ed Sykes/Allstar via Getty Images)

Declan Rice is reportedly close to agreeing a new contract with Arsenal which will see him bank a huge pay increase.

‌



‌



Rice's current deal is due to expire at the end of next season, but the Gunners have moved early to ward off any interest from their rivals. The midfielder joined the club in a £105million move from West Ham in the summer of 2023 and has become a lynchpin of Mikel Arteta's side.

‌



He has made 165 appearances for Arsenal, contributing 21 goals and 33 assists while helping them to win a first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

‌



His form has prompted Arsenal to enter into contract negotiations and BBC Sport reports that the talks have progressed well. Rice currently earns around £240,000 per week and is expected to jump close to the £350,000-a-week that Bukayo Saka takes home.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Saka is Arsenal's top-earner, having signed a new four-year contract in February. His new deal was followed by one for Arteta, who committed his future to the Gunners for another four years on Wednesday.

Arteta is now paid close to £20million per year, making him the best paid manager in the Premier League. Arsenal owners Stan and Josh Kroenke have been keen to secure their top talent and Rice is considered the next piece of the jigsaw.

“He can adapt to anything that you throw at him,” Arteta said of Rice's importance to the team last season. “But at the moment that forward thinking and anything that is in front of him is probably much more positive for the team.

‌



View 2 Images Declan Rice will move in line with Bukayo Saka after signing a new deal (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

"He has earned the right to increase that role, to be more and more important, to be very present in everything that we do.

“He’s in the leadership group, which is very important as well, and it’s a real presence. Sometimes you don’t need to just wear the armband to feel really connected, really powerful and really important in the team.”

‌



Rice missed the most recent England camp for the Nations League, but Thomas Tuchel was full of praise for him at the World Cup in the summer.

“He is one of the very best midfielders in the world," the England boss said. "He’s humble, ready to be a team player, ready to give quality and energy to the group. He learns every day in his career.”

Rice, who has 80 caps and eight goals for his country, has made seven appearances for Arsenal across all competitions this season.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson urges UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in a behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; there were allegations of spitting by an Israeli player at half-time, while the Israeli government criticised the Irish players for bowing their heads during the national anthem

Republic of Ireland: Heimir Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future after tense draw

Ireland's head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson has called for UEFA to keep his team and Israel separate in future

Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

The Ireland boss was speaking following his side's 1-1 UEFA Nations League draw with Israel behind closed doors in Serbia.

The games between the two nations this international break were overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

This continued in Serbia, as Ireland fitness coach Damien Doyle was allegedly spat on by an Israeli player at half-time, according to reports in the stadium.

Irish media reported that the incident took place as the teams went down the tunnel. Ireland boss Hallgrimsson confirmed there was an allegation, but he admitted he didn't see it and declined to comment further on it.

However, when asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Israeli Government accuses ROI of 'moral blindness'

The Israeli Government have accused the Ireland football team of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during their national anthem.

For the second time in a week, the Irish players, coaching team and FAI all bowed their heads while the Israeli national anthem was played pre-match.

Image: Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the national anthem

The official Israeli Government X account posted: "While some use the football field as their political theatre, for us this is personal.

"1939: Irish players raised their arms in salute to Nazi Germany.

"2026: Irish players bowed their heads during Israel's anthem.

"Different generations. The same moral blindness.

"Today, Israel's players wear black armbands to remember those brutally massacred by Hamas on October 7 - including former professional footballer Lior Asulin.

"Some of us have skin in the game. Others just make a show of it."

Sky Sports News has contacted the FAI for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged that a derogatory term had been used, which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. The term is not associated with antisemitic or anti-Israeli abuse.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying: "That's completely untrue," before bringing the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called following an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist, who said a microphone had been taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands that no further action was taken by police.

Sports.content:
Match report and reaction as Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in behind-closed-doors contest in Serbia; Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out after the break; sides clashed at half-time

Republic of Ireland 1-1 Israel: Troy Parrott scores again as sides draw second controversial Nations League meeting

The Republic of Ireland drew 1-1 with Israel in the second controversial Nations League fixture between the sides.

Troy Parrott's first-half penalty was cancelled out by Dor Peretz after the break in the behind-closed-doors game in Serbia.

The Republic's 'home' fixture was held on neutral territory at the 4,500-seat TSC arena in Backa Topola, due to "operational challenges that could impact on the delivery of the game on home soil" according to a June Football Association of Ireland (FAI) statement.

Both sides wore black armbands. The Republic's, the same as in Hungary to acknowledge - as the Football Association of Ireland chief David Courrell explained before that contest - "all lives lost" in the ongoing Israel-Hamas conflict.

Israel's armbands - which read "7.10" - were to commemorate the October 7, 2023 Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, their official X account confirmed.

The pitch featured no sponsored content or branding, just UEFA graphics with slogans like "football for all", a decision taken by the FAI.

Image: The referee pleads with the benches in Serbia

Tensions rose at half-time after a fracas broke out in front of the tunnel and players from both sides engaged in a heated argument, with the Israeli Government later accusing Irish players of "moral blindness" for bowing their heads during Israel's national anthem, as they did in Monday's first match.

Officials broke up a second altercation in three minutes of added time, and there were more heated words exchanged after the final whistle.

On the pitch Parrott, who has now scored 10 times in his last seven competitive internationals, fired the Republic in front from the spot in the 39th minute before Dor Peretz drew the sides level two minutes after the restart.

The result puts Ireland third in Nations League Group B3, level on points with second-placed Kosovo.

Hallgrimsson calls on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future

Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson has called on UEFA to keep Ireland and Israel apart in future.

Speaking after the 1-1 draw, Hallgrimsson also declined to comment on the half-time fracas between the two sides.

When asked if the two countries should be playing each other again, he told RTE Sport: "No, they shouldn't. That's not ours to decide - that's UEFA who decides that. Obviously, there's a big support for Palestine in Ireland. There's not many countries that support Palestine as much as Ireland does.

"I wouldn't wish any national team to go through what we've gone through in these two weeks, so maybe UEFA just needs to step in and do something."

On the half-time incident, he said in his post-match press conference: "I was there. I'm not going to comment on it. It's something that a disciplinary committee is probably going to look at."

Sky Sports News has contacted UEFA for comment.

Two Israeli journalists banned for post-match press conferences

Meanwhile, prior to the match, UEFA confirmed that two Israeli journalists were banned from the post-match press conferences, after Saturday's pre-match Ireland press conference descended into chaos.

The media access for Ireland was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed Irish players had racially abused them during the match in Hungary last weekend.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close.

After the press conference ended abruptly, Serbian police were called due to an allegation of assault by an Israeli journalist who had the microphone taken from them by an FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there was no further action was taken by police.

Sports.title: Ireland news conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland vs Israel is being played in Serbia as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott; protests briefly halted Ireland's draw with Austria on Thursday over opposition to Sunday's Israel fixture

Republic of Ireland vs Israel: Heimir Hallgrimsson's press conference cut short after tense exchanges with Israeli media

Republic of Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson's pre-match press conference ahead of Sunday's match against Israel in Serbia ended abruptly after a tense exchange with Israeli media.

The media access was cut short after an Israeli journalist alleged that Israeli players had claimed they were racially abused by Irish players during their match in Hungary last Sunday.

The journalist alleged a derogatory term was used - which Sky Sports has chosen not to repeat. It is not a term associated with being antisemitic or anti-Israeli.

An Irish press officer refuted the allegation, saying "that's completely untrue", and brought the news conference to a premature close as one of his colleagues remonstrated with the reporter.

Image: Ireland's players bowed their heads before facing Israel in the reverse fixture last week

Hallgrimsson later labelled the accusation a "verbal attack" during a separate briefing for members of the Irish press.

The exchange in the main press conference took place after Hallgrimsson was also asked a question about a co-pilot who attacked a pilot and tried to hijack a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv earlier this week.

The reporter's question was shut down by the FAI press officer.

Sky Sports News understands there are no open UEFA investigations at this stage from the previous meeting between Israel and Ireland last weekend.

The FAI are conducting their own investigation into whether striker Adam Idah was racially abused by Israeli supporters during their 3-0 UEFA Nations League win but have yet to make an official complaint to UEFA.

Image: Protesters interrupted Ireland's draw with Austria by throwing tennis balls onto the pitch with Palestine flags on them

Despite the high-profile nature of the fixture, members of the Irish media later reported that there was no UEFA delegate present at the news conference.

Sky Sports News was told a UEFA match delegate does not have to attend press conferences. The duty is left to the venue media manager, whose job it is to report anything if there is an incident.

Sunday's match is being played in Backa Topola, Serbia, as the FAI moved the game to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" in June following widespread calls for a boycott.

Sky Sports News has approached the FAI for comment.

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
