Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Challenges Emanuel Navarrete’s Dominant Image
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster believes Emanuel Navarrete’s destruction of Eduardo “Sugar” Nunez came against an opponent who couldn’t offer enough resistance, telling Lance Pugmire that the Mexican champion’s size helped him dominate.

Foster faces Navarrete in a super featherweight unification on October 24 in San Antonio. He acknowledges that Navarrete looked sharp against Nunez, but says he’ll present a different challenge.

“He looked sharp, but Nunez didn’t give us anything,” Foster told BoxingScene. “Nunez is too small. He was at 122lbs a couple years ago, so he’s a naturally smaller guy. When he tried to turn it up on Navarrete, he was too small. He couldn’t hurt him. Navarrete treated him like a little kid.”

Foster’s weight-history claim is inaccurate. Nunez’s last appearance near 122 pounds was in 2017, and he was slightly above that limit. More recent weight reports list him at 132.4 pounds against Oscar Escandon in 2023 and 133 against Miguel Marriaga in 2024. He was an established super featherweight champion when Navarrete beat him.

The stronger explanation is stylistic. Nunez is a straightforward slugger who gave Navarrete the kind of punching contest he thrives in. Navarrete proved better at it, overwhelming an opponent whose approach left him available for punishment.

That performance doesn’t erase the vulnerabilities exposed against Denys Berinchyk, Robson Conceicao and Charly Suarez. Berinchyk beat him at lightweight, while Conceicao and Suarez made his work difficult at 130. Navarrete can look destructive without being difficult to hit or impossible to outbox.

Foster’s opportunity is to make Navarrete work for his openings. Movement, counters, and changes of pace could force him into a less comfortable fight than Nunez provided. Trading for extended stretches would give away that advantage.

The uncertainty is whether Foster can sustain that discipline under pressure. His uneven majority-decision victory over Ray Ford leaves room for doubt.

Foster doesn’t need Nunez to have been undersized for his argument to work. He needs to demonstrate that Navarrete’s success against one slugger won’t translate against a champion offering a different style.

Sports.title: Shakur Stevenson Accepts Devin Haney’s 145-Pound Offer
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson has publicly accepted Devin Haney’s proposed 145-pound catchweight, moving their fight discussions forward after previously pushing for 144. The remaining question is whether Shakur has also dropped his request for a 10-pound rehydration limit.

“145.0 U GOT A DEAL DEEHOE!!!!” Shakur posted on X.

Haney quoted the post and responded: “Crown me #1 P4P after this InshaAllah.”

That exchange gives the negotiations something they previously lacked: both fighters publicly agreeing to the same contracted weight. It does not explain what happens after the official weigh-in, which has been another point of disagreement.

Haney’s earlier offer was 145 pounds with no rehydration clause for a December fight. Shakur had sought two restrictions: a catchweight below the 147-pound welterweight limit and a cap on how much weight Haney could regain afterward.

Shakur’s latest message addresses the first condition. He does not mention the second.

If Shakur is accepting Haney’s proposal in full, he would be conceding more than the extra pound. Haney could replenish without the 10-pound restriction Shakur had wanted, potentially giving him a larger size advantage when they enter the ring.

That was the reason behind Shakur’s earlier insistence on a cap. Coming up from 140 pounds, he wanted some control over the size of the opponent he would actually face. A 145-pound agreement alone would not provide that protection.

Haney’s pound-for-pound declaration also raises expectations for his own performance. He is already talking about the reward for beating Shakur, giving his rival another line to revisit if the fight happens and Haney falls short.

The next useful clarification needs to concern the rehydration terms. If that restriction has been removed, the teams have cleared an obstacle that went beyond their one-pound disagreement.

Until those details emerge, this is progress toward a fight, with Shakur accepting 145 and Haney welcoming the response. Neither supplied post announces a signed contract or confirms a date.

Sports.title: Vasiliy Lomachenko Targets Anthony Cacace Despite Title Commitments
Sports.content:
Vasiliy Lomachenko is targeting Anthony Cacace for a world title fight at 130 pounds, but the WBA champion’s existing commitments could force him to take another route for his comeback.

Lomachenko is reportedly targeting Cacace, according to Lance Pugmire, but the champion is scheduled to defend against Nick Ball on December 19 in Belfast. That leaves Lomachenko looking toward a fighter who already has an opponent, with another title obligation waiting afterward.

The attraction is clear. Lomachenko wants to become undisputed at super featherweight, and Cacace holds the WBA belt he would need. However, identifying the desired opponent is easier than finding room in that opponent’s schedule.

The WBA has authorized Cacace to make a voluntary defense before the end of the year, then requires the winner to face Elnur Samedov. Even if Cacace beats Ball, Lomachenko cannot assume he will get the next opportunity. Samedov’s position would have to be addressed before that fight could happen.

Meanwhile, Boxing News reported on October 2 that Lomachenko’s return is being planned for November 20 in Las Vegas. The report named no opponent, making Cacace look more like a subsequent target than the man waiting for him in his first fight back.

That could be a useful approach for Lomachenko. Returning at 130 would give him an opportunity to see how he performs at the lower weight after his lengthy absence before committing to a championship fight. It would also give his team time to see whether Cacace retains the belt.

The difficulty is the waiting. A comeback bout would address Lomachenko’s inactivity, but it would not resolve the WBA title queue. He could win his return and still need another fight while Cacace or Ball handles Samedov.

Lomachenko’s undisputed ambition gives the comeback a purpose. Whether he can pursue it quickly depends on access to the champions, and Cacace’s schedule already presents an obstacle.

Sports.title: Jermall Charlo Suffers Camp Injury, Scratched from Fundora Undercard
Sports.content:
Jermall Charlo hit another roadblock in his comeback effort after suffering a training injury, knocking him off the October 17 card where he was set to face Koen Mazoudier, per Mike Coppinger. At 36, the former two-division champ loses critical ground after sitting on the shelf for nearly 17 months.

Jose Resendiz steps in to replace Charlo in the 10-round contest on the Sebastian Fundora versus Ermal Hadribeaj undercard. Specifics on Charlo’s injury remain undisclosed, with no timeline offered for a rescheduled bout.

Charlo last appeared in May 2025, halting Thomas LaManna in six rounds. Prior to that outing, he topped Jose Benavidez Jr. in November 2023 following a 29-month layoff. Those represent his only two ring walks since outpointing Juan Macias Montiel back in June 2021.

That sporadic schedule leaves Charlo severely depleted of momentum as he tries carving out a campaign at 168 pounds. The Mazoudier pairing was designed to bank rounds, shake off rust, and set up a meaningful fight. That starting block is gone for now.

A pristine 34-0 record with 23 stoppages still provides promotional leverage, yet numbers on paper cannot reveal what remains of his prime form. Halting LaManna served a purpose, but letting another massive gap follow erased any genuine rhythm he had generated.

Pinning the physical setback on ring age or rust is pure guesswork since details remain scarce. The end result speaks for itself: another fight date evaporates while the clock keeps ticking on his career.

Sporadic showcase wins will not move the needle if every outing leads right back into hibernation. Charlo needs consistent rounds under the lights to prove he can handle upper-tier contenders and justify a major title shot. You simply cannot treat a boxing career like an occasional hobby and expect the human body to cooperate when you suddenly demand championship level intensity in camp.

When a 36-year-old fighter sits out for nearly 17 months after already logging only two fights in over five years, the connective tissue, joints, and muscular endurance are nowhere near adapted to the grind. Taking an aging fighter from zero to full throttle in a hard training camp is practically an invitation for a breakdown.

Mazoudier was lined up to jump-start that momentum. Instead, Resendiz gets the work on October 17, leaving Charlo stuck on the sidelines waiting to discover what he has left in the tank.

Sports.title: Anthony Yarde Claims Ben Whittaker Team Wanted Another Year
Sports.content:
Anthony Yarde claims Ben Whittaker’s team wanted another year before putting the two together, despite Eddie Hearn now including him among the options for Whittaker’s next fight.

Yarde is willing to accept the bout immediately. His account of the earlier discussions adds a different perspective to Hearn’s proposed route after Whittaker’s difficult finish against Conor Wallace.

“Personally, we tried to get that fight, and then his team came back and said he would need another year. He’s still in that stage where he’s growing and he’s learning and all these kind of things. But if that fight got offered to me tomorrow, I’ll take it,” Yarde told talkSPORT Boxing.

Yarde didn’t specify when those discussions took place, so his comments don’t establish that Whittaker’s team is currently rejecting the fight. Hearn naming him as a possibility also falls short of an offer.

The concern is whether Whittaker is ready for that step. Hearn included Yarde, the Joshua Buatsi–Willy Hutchinson winner and a Wallace rematch, among his options, while acknowledging that Ben needs another fight before moving toward Dmitry Bivol.

Choosing Yarde would ask considerably more of Whittaker than running it back with Wallace. Yarde has faced Sergey Kovalev, Artur Beterbiev, and David Benavidez. He would enter with experience of the pressure and punishment that comes with fighting elite light heavyweights.

Whittaker’s early control against Wallace showed his ability to win rounds with speed and accuracy. The closing rounds left questions about how well he can maintain that work when hurt or exhausted. Yarde would have reason to keep testing him even if Ben built an early lead.

Yarde was measured about the matchup, describing Whittaker as “fantastic over six rounds” and insisting he would take him seriously. That makes this an awkward choice for Hearn: a recognizable opponent who welcomes the fight, but one capable of testing the very weaknesses Ben’s last performance exposed.

Sports.title: Israil Madrimov Returns October 30 Against Seymur Isayev
Sports.content:
Israil Madrimov gets back to work on October 30 at Humo Arena in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, taking on Seymur Isayev after another lengthy stretch of inactivity. The Uzbekistan Professional Boxing Federation confirmed the booking, per Sports.kz.

This marks just the second ring appearance for the former WBA junior middleweight champion since dropping tough decision losses to Terence Crawford then Vergil Ortiz Jr. Madrimov took care of business against Luis David Salazar back in January. Still, sitting out for nine months right after that win stalled his momentum toward the division belt holders.

Isayev brings a southpaw stance from Azerbaijan into the biggest test of his career. He rides a string of knockout victories, but stepping into Tashkent against an elite operator like Madrimov represents an entirely different level of competition.

Madrimov gets a prime opportunity to showcase his skills in front of his hometown supporters. Whether that victory actually pushes him toward the top contenders at 154 pounds really hinges on his performance plus how fast his team lines up the next assignment.

Madrimov secured world championship status by halting Magomed Kurbanov in 2024. Crawford took the belt later that summer, with the Ortiz defeat arriving in February 2025. Those setbacks came against the absolute best fighters in boxing, so they never completely booted him from title relevance.

Health troubles also disrupted his schedule. He struggled with bronchitis that spiraled into pneumonia around the Ortiz bout, followed by surgeries on his shoulder along with his knee. That ordeal kept him out of action for roughly eleven months before he defeated Salazar.

Nobody has officially explained the reason for the latest delay. We have a confirmed fight date now, though nothing points to another physical setback.

Madrimov wants to turn his earlier victory into real traction. Putting on a clinic against Isayev will help, but another long vacation right afterward keeps him running in place. He needs this hometown showcase to serve as a launchpad. Madrimov is 31 years old with only 14 professional bouts under his belt, so running a once-a-year schedule is boxing suicide for a guy trying to claw back into championship contention.

At 154 pounds, the division moves too fast to sit on the shelf for eight or nine months between tune-ups. When an ex-champion drops back-to-back decision losses to the very top tier, taking almost a year off just to beat Luis David Salazar, and then disappearing for another nine months before fighting an unproven Seymur Isayev, all momentum disappears.

A four-fight schedule would force mandatory activity, keep him sharp, and put him in front of the sanctioning bodies every three months. Even if two of those dates are quick stay-busy showcases against guys he can blast out early, it builds the fight frequency he desperately lacks. Right now, by the time he gets through two prolonged training camps and unexplained layoffs, another year has evaporated, and the younger contenders pass him by.

If he does not start fighting every three to four months, his physical prime will be completely gone before he ever touches another major purse or world title shot.

Sports.title: Sebastian Fundora Claims More Toughness Than Jaron Ennis
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora feels he has more dog in him than Jaron Ennis. He plans to use relentless pressure alongside nonstop punching to neutralize what makes Boots lethal at 154 pounds.

Fundora wants a unification clash right after his October 17 defense against Ermal Hadribeaj. Ennis sits near the top of his target list, with Fundora already visualizing his battle plan.

“Pain, man. We bring the pain. I know I could beat him,” Fundora said to Sean Zittel. “Whether it is our awkward style that everybody loves to say or the fact that we throw a lot of punches, but we definitely have, I think we have more dog in us.”

When Zittel noted that Ennis proved his grit before, Fundora didn’t budge.

“That is fine, man. That is fine. Well, you showed it for like a round. I have been showing it my whole career.”

Fundora clearly believes he can drag Ennis into the trenches. Firing continuous punches could push Boots past his comfort zone, especially if Fundora unloads immediately after Ennis finishes flurrying.

That strategy cuts both ways. Stepping inside opens clean lanes for Ennis to time nasty counters. Fundora might gladly trade leather, but absorbing heavy shots eventually drains anyone trying to march forward.

The real test comes down to controlling the pace. Boots doesn’t need to sit in the pocket just to prove his chin. If he slips off the center line, he can crack Fundora before the big man ever finds his rhythm.

Fundora’s attitude injects genuine heat into this potential matchup. He wants to test the challenger on pure grit, finding out what happens when Boots faces someone who never stops pressing forward.

Nothing is signed yet. Fundora has to take care of business against Hadribeaj first, but he’s already put Boots on notice if unification happens.

Sports.title: Janibek Alimkhanuly and Jacob Bank Agree Title Fight
Sports.content:
Janibek Alimkhanuly found his path to a 168-pound crown after Hamzah Sheeraz vacated the belt instead of facing him. The Kazakh southpaw will battle Denmark’s Jacob Bank for the vacant WBO super middleweight championship after both camps reached an agreement.

WBO president Gustavo Olivieri confirmed the deal on X Wednesday. An official date along with a host location will arrive soon, as both camps formally notified the sanctioning organization that terms are locked in without needing a purse bid.

Olivieri stated that the WBO received formal written notification from Team Zhanibek Alimkhanuly plus Team Jacob Bank that both sides settled terms to contest the vacant crown, with further details coming in due course.

Sheeraz’s exit shuffled the deck for Janibek, yet the prize remains intact. Rather than hunting down the British titlist, the former unified middleweight kingpin squares off with a fresh, hungry challenger aiming for his first world championship. The sanctioning body initially ordered talks between top contender Janibek and the third-ranked Bank as soon as the belt opened up.

Bank comes into the fight sporting an unblemished record featuring 20 victories, 11 coming inside the distance. The Danish contender stayed busy with three wins already in 2026, creating genuine momentum heading into the biggest night of his career. Taking on an elite southpaw who ruled the 160-pound division demands everything he has.

Stepping up to super middleweight brings real curiosity for Janibek. Dominating middleweight proved his pedigree, but he must prove his firepower carries into a heavier weight category. Bank brings size, hunger, plus momentum to make life rough for the favorite.

Claiming this vacant belt crowns Janibek as a two-division champion. He kept his title shot alive after Sheeraz walked away, so taking care of Bank seals the mission.

If Janibek collects the WBO belt, he instantly becomes one of the highest-risk, lowest-reward targets in the entire division. He may have to rely on sanctioning body mandatories or take on the top contenders from Europe to get anyone to sign on the dotted line.

Ghana News.title: Gov’t will not curb free speech under Mahama – Kwakye Ofosu
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Government Communications, Felix Kwakye Ofosu, has dismissed claims that the government is restricting freedom of expression, insisting that legitimate criticism must be distinguished from criminal conduct.

His comments come amid concerns about Ghana’s democratic freedoms, including criticism surrounding the recent arrest of nurse Salomey Baffoe Awiti in Techiman.

Speaking at the launch of the 30th GJA Media Awards, Mr Kwakye Ofosu said the government had no intention of interfering with legitimate free expression, but argued that law enforcement must act where social media activity crosses into conduct that threatens public peace.

He said some individuals had previously used social media to spread hate speech and commentary capable of worsening conflicts in parts of the country.

“Africa is littered with examples of how speech like that led to serious genocide and conflict. And it will be derelict on the part of law enforcement to sit and not do anything about people who abuse the space of social media to engage in these sorts of activities,” he said.

Mr Kwakye Ofosu said law enforcement had used available technology to identify and address such activities, but stressed that such interventions should not be interpreted as a crackdown on free speech.

“Also, a clear distinction must be struck between free speech and criminal conduct. Under no circumstances will the government of President John Dramani Mahama curb free speech,” he said.

Ghana News.title: NDPC, UNIDO discuss new partnership to drive Ghana’s industrial development
Ghana News.content:
The National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) are exploring a new partnership to better align industrial development interventions with Ghana’s national priorities.

The discussions centre on a new five-year Programme for Country Partnership (PCP) that UNIDO plans to introduce in Ghana from 2027. The programme is expected to provide a framework for UNIDO’s support to the country’s industrial development agenda, with consultations planned with key government institutions and other stakeholders.

UNIDO Country Representative in Ghana, Dr Emmanuel Kalenzi, said the proposed partnership would strengthen the organisation’s relationship with the NDPC and deepen its understanding of the Commission’s role in national development planning.

He described the NDPC as a key national partner and stressed the importance of ensuring that UNIDO interventions respond to Ghana’s development priorities and existing planning frameworks.

The proposed areas of focus include agro-industrial value chains and industrial parks, support for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, job creation, investment promotion and trade, industrial policy and skills development.

The programme is also expected to cover the circular economy, renewable energy and energy efficiency.

Dr Kalenzi outlined the plans when a UNIDO delegation paid a courtesy call on the NDPC on Monday, October 5, 2026. The engagement provided an opportunity for both institutions to identify areas where closer collaboration could support Ghana’s industrial transformation.

NDPC Director-General, Dr Audrey Smock Amoah, welcomed the initiative and expressed the Commission’s readiness to support the development of the proposed programme.

She said closer coordination between national planning institutions and development partners would help ensure that external interventions are aligned with Ghana’s broader development objectives.

The proposed PCP will subsequently be developed through consultations with relevant national institutions, with the outcome expected to guide UNIDO’s industrial development support in Ghana from 2027.

Ghana News.title: Mahama Ayariga calls for innovative financing to make housing more affordable
Ghana News.content:
Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga

Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, says Ghana’s housing challenge cannot be addressed through construction alone, with innovative and sustainable financing needed to make decent homes more accessible.

He said affordable housing requires financing models that can respond to the needs of ordinary Ghanaians, particularly those who may struggle to meet the cost of conventional mortgage arrangements.

Mr Ayariga made the remarks in a Facebook post on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, after participating in the National Conference on Housing Finance 2026, where stakeholders discussed measures to improve access to housing.

He said the discussions focused on affordable mortgage financing, mobilising long-term capital and developing sustainable housing solutions. According to him, addressing the financing gap is essential to creating a housing system that is more inclusive and accessible to a wider section of the population.

The Minister said the government would continue engaging stakeholders on practical approaches to housing finance as part of efforts to create a more inclusive housing future for Ghana.

Ghana News.title: NDPC reviews 22-year-old guidelines for regional, district planning units
Ghana News.content:
The National Development Planning Commission (NDPC) has begun a nationwide review of the guidelines governing Regional Planning Coordinating Units (RPCUs) and District Planning Coordinating Units (DPCUs), as part of efforts to align decentralised development planning with current institutional and technological realities.

The review, supported by GIZ’s PAIRed programme, is examining the existing guidelines and gathering input from officials responsible for development planning at the regional and district levels.

The consultations are expected to identify implementation gaps and generate practical recommendations for improving planning, coordination, monitoring and reporting.

The existing guidelines were developed in 2004, and Chief Director of the Greater Accra Regional Coordinating Council, Rev. Harry Nii Kwatei Owoo, said significant changes since then had made an update necessary.

He cited developments in the legal and institutional framework, planning and budgeting processes, monitoring requirements and the growing use of digital systems in public administration.

Speaking at the Greater Accra engagement on Tuesday, October 6, Rev. Owoo urged participants to draw on their experiences to identify gaps in the current guidelines and propose measures that would make the revised document more responsive to the realities of regional and district planning.

NDPC Director-General Dr Audrey Smock Amoah said the review must be grounded in the practical experiences of officials working within the decentralised planning system.

She said it provides an opportunity to align the guidelines with current institutional arrangements, planning requirements and technological developments, while addressing challenges affecting their implementation.

Dr Amoah also stressed the need for regional and district authorities to prepare and submit development plans and annual progress reports on time, warning that delays at those levels can affect national development planning, monitoring and reporting.

The nationwide consultations began on October 5 with engagements in the Upper East and Central Regions, with Greater Accra forming part of the second day of the exercise.

The consultations will continue across the country, with stakeholder feedback expected to inform the finalisation of the revised RPCU and DPCU guidelines.

The process is being supported by GIZ’s PAIRed programme, an initiative commissioned by Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union in Ghana and the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), and implemented by GIZ in partnership with the Ministry of Finance.

Ghana News.title: Ghana to champion ECOWAS adoption of Accra Convention on cargo documents – Trade Minister
Ghana News.content:
Ghana is positioning itself to lead efforts within ECOWAS to adopt and implement a new international framework aimed at making trade finance and cross-border movement of goods easier through negotiable cargo documents.

The Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, said Ghana is committed to signing and ratifying the United Nations Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents, which is expected to provide a common legal framework for the use of cargo documents in financing and trading goods transported by road, rail and air.

She made the commitment on Wednesday, October 7, 2026, when she opened a virtual sensitisation programme organised for ECOWAS Member States on the Convention.

The programme was intended to help countries examine the implications of the instrument and assess its compatibility with their respective national legal systems.

The Convention was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on December 15, 2025, through Resolution 80/162, and is recommended to be known as the Accra Convention on Negotiable Cargo Documents.

It is scheduled to be opened for signature in Accra on October 26, 2026, giving Ghana an opportunity to host the next stage of efforts towards its adoption.

Ms Ofosu-Adjare urged participating ECOWAS countries to use the sensitisation programme to deepen their understanding of the Convention and submit clear recommendations to their respective governments on the way forward.

She said Ghana was ready to welcome ECOWAS Member States and stakeholders from across the world to Accra for the signing ceremony.

The Secretary of the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL), Anna Joubin-Bret, and ECOWAS Commission Director of Trade, Kolawole Sofola, also encouraged Member States and other stakeholders to participate actively in the process and support the Convention’s signature, ratification and implementation.

Ghana News.title: NHIS coverage rises from 57% to about 70% in less than two years under Mahama — Health Minister
Ghana News.content:
Coverage under Ghana’s National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) has increased from 57 per cent to about 70 per cent in less than two years, Health Minister Kwabena Mintah Akandoh has said.

He attributed the increase to measures aimed at strengthening the scheme’s finances, including the uncapping of the National Health Insurance Levy. Mr Akandoh said the additional resources had improved the NHIS’s ability to meet its obligations to healthcare providers.

“We’re strengthening what we have come to meet. We took the NHIS from 57%; as I speak to you now, it’s about 70%. In a matter of less than two years,” he said at the Ministry of Health’s Sector Update Engagement in Accra on Wednesday, October 7.

The Minister said funding for the scheme had risen from about GH¢6.5 billion in 2024 to GH¢9.8 billion in 2025, allowing government to increase payments to healthcare providers by an average of 50 per cent.

He said the higher payments were intended to reduce delays in settling claims owed to healthcare facilities and improve their capacity to continue providing services to NHIS beneficiaries.

Mr Akandoh maintained that improving the scheme’s financial position and ensuring timely reimbursement to service providers were critical to sustaining access to healthcare and reducing financial pressure on beneficiaries.

Ghana News.title: BRICS membership could give Ghana more options in global diplomacy — analyst
Ghana News.content:
Dr. Nana Yaw Mireku

Ghana could gain greater room to manoeuvre in an increasingly fragmented global order if it joins the BRICS grouping, International Relations Analyst Dr Nana Yaw Mireku has said.

He said membership would give Ghana an opportunity to widen its diplomatic and economic engagements beyond its traditional Western partners, while allowing the country to pursue its interests across a broader range of international relationships.

“One card that you are likely to score from being a member of BRICS is options,” Dr Mireku said on Citi FM on Wednesday, October 7, 2026. “What it means is that in these changing geopolitical dynamics, if you are a member of BRICS, it gives you options to interact, to negotiate globally beyond looking at a Western corridor or the Western window.”

His comments followed Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa’s indication that Ghana intends to submit an application to join BRICS as the government explores ways to diversify its international partnerships, expand economic opportunities and deepen cooperation with countries in the Global South.

Dr Mireku said Ghana’s foreign policy should remain anchored in national interest rather than exclusive alignment with any geopolitical bloc. “In the pursuit of our national interest, we do not have to be tied to a particular geopolitical block,” he said.

He noted that BRICS includes major emerging economies such as China, India, Brazil and South Africa, which could provide Ghana with additional avenues for diplomatic and economic engagement.

The analyst, however, cautioned against viewing membership as an automatic guarantee of access to new markets or financial opportunities. “It does not mean that once you are a member of BRICS, automatically these countries open their markets up to you,” he said.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod sells $125m to commercial banks in maiden FX auction
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) has sold approximately US$125 million to commercial banks in its maiden foreign exchange auction under its new spot FX sales and intermediation framework.

JOYBUSINESS understands that the auction was conducted on Tuesday as part of efforts to strengthen transparency, fairness and regulatory compliance in the foreign exchange market.

The auction forms part of GoldBod’s plan to provide commercial banks with more predictable and transparent access to US dollars through its GoldBod GoFX platform.

$1bn FX Sales to Banks

GoldBod earlier announced plans to sell US$1 billion to commercial banks during the month to support stability in the foreign exchange market.

The GoldBod programme is expected to generate about US$1.5 billion in total.

Of this amount, US$1 billion will be sold to commercial banks, while the remaining US$500 million will be advanced to the Bank of Ghana to support the accumulation of foreign exchange reserves.

Twice-Weekly FX Sales

Under the new framework, GoldBod will conduct foreign exchange sales twice a week, on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

Participating banks will submit their requests during a designated sales window.

Where demand exceeds the available FX tranche, GoldBod said allocations will be made on a pro-rata basis to ensure a transparent and equitable distribution of the available foreign exchange.

Transactions will be settled on the same day.

The US dollar leg will be completed by 3:00pm, while the Ghana cedi leg will be completed by 4:00pm.

Measures to Prevent Speculation

GoldBod said participating banks will be required to declare that their requests are backed by actual unmet foreign exchange demand or evidence of a short position.

The banks will also be required to comply with Bank of Ghana regulations and directives.

The measures are intended to ensure that the facility responds to genuine market demand and is not used for speculative purposes.

BoG to Provide Regulatory Oversight

The programme will operate under the regulatory oversight of the Bank of Ghana.

GoldBod said the central bank will have real-time access to the GoldBod GoFX platform.

GoldBod will also submit transaction reports to the Bank of Ghana after each sale.

The GoFX platform provides electronic submission and allocation processing, as well as time-stamping, transaction histories and audit trails.

According to GoldBod, these features are designed to strengthen transparency, accountability and post-trade verification.

The details were provided at a meeting between GoldBod and commercial banks ahead of the rollout of the new Spot FX Sales and Intermediation Framework.

The framework is expected to provide authorised commercial banks with predictable and transparent access to US dollars through the GoldBod GoFX platform.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Why single Ebola death in Kenya has sparked fears of wider African spread
World.content:
According to the WHO, the Kenyan patient first got sick in the DRC, where they had been living, and was treated there.

Share Why single Ebola death in Kenya has prompted fears of wider African spread on social media

Kenya reported its first death from a deadly strain of Ebola virus which had spread widely, starting in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) earlier this year.

The Bundibugyo (BDBV) strain of Ebola was first detected in Uganda in 2007, according to the WHO. The ongoing outbreak in the DRC has killed at least 4,148 people out of 8,300 reported cases. It also spread across the border to Uganda, which had about 20 cases before being declared Ebola-free in July.

However, the person who died in Kenya from the disease had travelled from the DRC to Uganda over land before taking a flight to Nairobi, raising questions about Uganda’s status as “Ebola-free”, concerns about the rigidity of Kenya’s screening processes for people coming into the country and fears that Ebola may have spread further than previously thought.

On Tuesday, the World Health Organization said the Kenyan government is now enhancing its disease surveillance with more targeted screening at high-risk points of entry.

But Wolfgang Preiser, a professor and head of medical virology at Stellenbosch University in South Africa, explained that while efforts are being made to bring the outbreak under control, it has grown so much that “sheer numbers and the speed of spread are overwhelming for many systems.

“I am not surprised that cases have reached other provinces in DRC and neighbouring countries. I expect that this will continue to happen until such time that the trajectory has been reversed and case numbers are in decline,” he told Al Jazeera.



Here’s what we know:

What is Ebola?

It is a serious, potentially deadly viral infection which can be caught when a person comes into contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person or wild animal, including fluid lingering on surfaces. People have also been known to contract the disease through eating contaminated meat.

There have been many outbreaks in Central, West and East Africa.

A West African outbreak from 2014 to 2016 killed at least 11,300 people of a reported 28,600 cases and accelerated the push to develop a vaccine. That was a different strain of the Ebola virus, known as Zaire, for which there is now a vaccine.

The strain behind the latest outbreak is Bundibugyo virus (BDBV), which is believed to have been caused by a new transmission from animals to humans, before then spreading between humans, rather than by variants linked to earlier outbreaks. There is no vaccine for Bundibugyo.

Symptoms can appear between two and 21 days after infection and can start suddenly with flu-like symptoms, including a high temperature, fatigue, and a headache. It can lead to internal and external bleeding, impaired liver and kidney function and organ failure.

How did this case of Ebola reach Kenya?

Kenyan Health Minister Aden Duale told reporters that the Kenyan patient, who has not been named, first became sick one month ago in the DRC, where they had been living for several years, and was treated there.

On October 2, the patient travelled by road to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, via Beni, then flew to Nairobi, arriving the next day.

After he arrived at the airport in Kenya, a relative and a friend took him to a hospital, where he was quickly isolated, and tests showed he had the virus, Duale said. Despite receiving care, the patient died from the virus on Monday and was buried on Tuesday in line with the country’s Ebola protocol.

So far, health authorities in Kenya have identified 28 potential contacts, including family members and health workers who cared for the infected patient. Authorities are also separately tracking 23 passengers and four crew members from his flight, “with arrangements under way for appropriate follow-up and quarantine of people assessed to be at risk”, the WHO reported.

Jean Bisimwa Nachega, a professor in infectious diseases at Stellenbosch University, emphasised that the virus does not “re

spect national borders”.

“Population mobility, displacement, cross-border trade, and fragile healthcare systems make containment particularly challenging. In eastern DRC, ongoing insecurity further complicates surveillance, contact tracing, and access to affected communities,” he told Al Jazeera.



“Regional cooperation is therefore essential.”

How did a sick patient get past screening in Uganda and Kenya?

Passengers travelling to, from or through Uganda and Kenya must pass multiple airport temperature checks and complete at least two digital forms intended to flag any potential exposure to the virus in the DRC. Somehow, the infected person in this case was missed by these checks.

Ugandan government spokesperson Alan Kasujja said Kampala was not to blame for the Kenyan man catching the virus and wrote on X, “Leave Uganda out of this conversation. We don’t have Ebola here.”

In a statement issued Tuesday, the Ugandan Ministry of Health said the man had a “normal temperature” when he was screened at Entebbe airport before his departure.

Kenyan authorities say he may have taken medication to mask his symptoms when he was later screened at Nairobi airport. Investigations are continuing, however.

“We are trying to retrieve the digital form he would have filled out at Entebbe airport when he went through the thermal scanning process to see what he declared in that form. The form includes questions about recent health problems but also whether a traveller was recently in DRC,” Richard Mugahi, a senior Ugandan health official, told the Reuters news agency.

“We are also going through airport security camera footage to see if we can identify the driver who dropped him at the airport so we can trace any contacts here.”

Preiser, the medical virology professor, also said the tracking system “seems to work as it did in Uganda”, with a diagnosis made rapidly as soon as the patient sought care in Kenya.

“It will be instructive to try and trace back what happened at the various stops during his travels, and lessons should be heeded by all countries,” he said.

He cited an example from a previous Ebola outbreak in West Africa, when a “British nurse fell sick during her return trip to the UK and reported to the medical check in Heathrow, only to be sent onwards to her destination where she was diagnosed with Ebola”.

The lesson, he said, was that “even cooperative travellers and good systems may fall through the net.”

Where else has Ebola spread?

Since it began in the DRC’s northeastern Ituri province, the latest outbreak has spread this year to seven provinces in the country’s north and east. It was officially declared an outbreak in the DRC in May.

Weak infrastructure, the remoteness of the region in eastern DRC, and ongoing conflict with armed groups near the borders with South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda have hindered efforts to respond to cases quickly and effectively.

Several factors have further complicated the response to the outbreak, including strikes by unpaid health workers, misinformation and cultural traditions. These have included open-coffin family burials of several of those killed by the virus earlier during the outbreak, potentially increasing the risk of further transmission.

The United Nations reported on October 2 that an Ebola-hit camp housing a transit centre for infected patients was burned by soldiers earlier this week when they were looking for weapons on the outskirts of Bunia, the capital city of Ituri province, which is at the epicentre of the outbreak.



The incident forced 19,000 people to flee the camp.

The disease also spread to Uganda, where 20 people who had travelled from the DRC were treated before the country declared it was free of Ebola in July.

Recently, it has become increasingly hard to contain within the DRC.

On Monday, Doctors Without Borders, known by its French initials MSF, warned that there had been an “alarming surge” of cases in eastern North Kivu province, which borders Uganda, and where 40 percent of new cases are currently being recorded.

“It is like fighting a megafire,” Stephanie Hoffmann, coordinator at MSF’s Ebola treatment centre in the city of Butembo, said. “Multiple outbreaks are developing at the same time, with varying intensity and in different locations.”

Some two million people live in North Kivu’s city of Butembo and surrounding areas, but it has only four Ebola treatment centres, two of which opened recently, MSF told the media. Patients often have to be transferred elsewhere, increasing the risk of infection to others, Hoffmann said.

What happens now?

The WHO is working with Kenyan authorities to trace contacts and strengthen checks for travellers coming into the country.

Mohamed Janabi, WHO regional director for Africa, said on Tuesday that “health emergency preparedness gives us a head start.

“Kenya has put important outbreak control measures in place. The priority now is to move swiftly to detect any further cases before the virus has an opportunity to spread. We’re supporting the ongoing efforts to strengthen the response, and with rapid and coordinated action, we can prevent the virus from gaining a foothold and stop a potential larger outbreak,” Janabi said.

The agency also said it has delivered about 1,000 Ebola tests and “1,000 personal protective equipment kits to high-risk counties in Kenya”.

In June, the Kenyan government granted the United States permission to set up an Ebola quarantine facility at the Laikipia airbase, 193km (120 miles) from the capital, Nairobi, to treat infected Americans travelling from African nations before they arrived in the US. The scheme generated uproar from locals who feared transmission of the disease, and Kenyan courts halted the plan.

Overall, Nachega said strengthening border screening wasn’t enough. It was also important to “reinforce the entire public health response”.

“This means training front-line healthcare workers, ensuring rapid laboratory diagnosis, promptly isolating suspected cases, and tracing and monitoring contacts. Kenya’s ability to identify this case provides an important opportunity to strengthen preparedness,” he added.

World.title: Protesters in Colombia rally against ties with Israel
World.content:
Hundreds took to the streets of Bogota to protest the ongoing genocide in Gaza.

Share Protesters in Colombia rally against ties with Israel on social media

Protesters have rallied in Colombia’s capital opposing the new far-right government’s policy towards Israel.

Hundreds took to the streets of Bogota on Wednesday to protest against the ongoing genocide in Gaza and the Colombian government’s decision to restore diplomatic and economic relations with Israel.

The protesters, who began their rally in front of the Israeli embassy in Bogota, criticised President Abelardo de la Espriella’s decision to open a new Colombian embassy in Jerusalem.

The rally marked three years since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, which were followed by Israel launching a genocidal war on Gaza.

“When diplomatic relations with Israel were broken off, the message was that we would not be a nation complicit in their atrocities,” Nicolas Isaza, who took part in the protest, told Al Jazeera.

“Today our government is no longer drawing a line against the atrocities being committed in Palestine,” he added.

De la Espriella, who was sworn in as president in August, promised close relations with the US and Israel during his election campaign as a way to combat armed groups in his country.

Colombia’s government has since restored relations with Israel after former President Gustavo Petro, who criticised Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza, severed diplomatic relations and halted Israeli arms imports.

The Colombian government also recognised Israel’s claim of sovereignty over the occupied Syrian Golan Heights, just days after the new president took power.

World.title: Signage at UK consulate in East Jerusalem removed as Israel’s deadline over
World.content:
Thursday marks 30 days since Israel’s foreign minister ordered the closure of the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem.

Share Signage at UK consulate in East Jerusalem removed as Israel’s deadline over on social media

Workers at the UK consulate in occupied East Jerusalem have removed its signage as the Israeli shutdown deadline arrives, further damaging strained ties between allies.

Journalists from the Reuters news agency saw ‌workers remove a plaque reading “British Consulate General” from the building on Thursday, as well as another sign for its consular section. The UK flag was still flying over the building.

Thursday marks 30 days since Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar ordered the closure of the consulate in occupied East Jerusalem. The move was in response to the UK’s wave of sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements, including a ban on importing goods made there.

The United Nations and most countries consider the settlements illegal under international law. Israel disputes this.

The United Kingdom threatened to expel 27 Israeli diplomats if Israel proceeded to close the consulate in occupied East Jerusalem, according to unverified Israeli media reports.

The consulate has not responded to an immediate request for comment.

Israel has been adamant the consulate will close even as the UK has sought to keep it open, including sending the country’s top national security adviser to Israel last week for talks.

The UK’s presence in the city dates back almost 200 years, long before the state of Israel was established in 1948. The closure order does not affect the UK’s embassy in Tel Aviv, which handles diplomatic relations with Israel’s government.

The consulate, in the Sheikh Jarrah neighbourhood of occupied East Jerusalem, handles the UK’s relations with Palestinians in Jerusalem, as well as in ‌the occupied West ⁠Bank and Gaza. It also provides consular services to Palestinians.



The UK Foreign Office on Wednesday declined to comment when asked whether the consulate was still operating or if diplomats working there had returned to the UK.

Despite the current strains, the ⁠UK and Israel are close economic, security and intelligence partners.

At least 10 protesters were removed from a Trump rally in San Antonio as he was heckled while campaigning for Republican Senate nominee Ken Paxton. Trump mocked the protesters, claiming without evidence they were paid, as supporters booed.

World.title: South Korea pledges legal action over alleged fuel exports to Russia
World.content:
Ukrainian reports of South Korean fuel exports to Russia come amid strained tensions between Seoul and Kyiv.

South Korea’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has said the government will take legal action over illegal fuel shipments to Russia if allegations from an adviser to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are confirmed.

The Foreign Ministry said on Thursday it had not confirmed whether South Korean fuel, including diesel, had been exported to Russia.

It added that exports of some products, such as diesel and jet fuel for commercial purposes, were not included in a South Korean exports control list to Russia.

On Wednesday, the South Korean presidential office dismissed a statement by Vladyslav Vlasiuk, an adviser to the Ukrainian president on sanctions policy, that 176,000 tonnes of fuel were shipped from South Korea to Russia via sanctioned tankers in July and August.

Ukraine’s top sanctions official said the alleged findings run counter to South Korea’s sanctions policy towards Russia.

“Since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, our government has consistently implemented sanctions and export controls against Russia in close cooperation with the international community,” South Korean presidential spokesperson Kang Yu-jung said on Wednesday, according to the Yonhap news agency.

“We ask that Ukraine also refrain from distorting the relevant policies of the Republic of Korea without sufficient verification of the facts and making public remarks that can damage international trust,” she added.

Relations between South Korea and Ukraine have been strained for the past couple of weeks after Seoul accused Zelenskyy of having “unilaterally disclosed” to the United Nations General Assembly that Kyiv had transferred two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea.



Seoul Korea demanded an official apology from Kyiv, claiming the Ukrainian president had breached a non-disclosure agreement. Kyiv said no such agreement was in place.

Pyongyang and Moscow, meanwhile, have deep ties, with the two countries having signed a mutual defence treaty in 2024. According to Ukrainian and South Korean estimates, about 14,000 to 15,000 North Korean soldiers were sent to support Russia’s war efforts against Ukraine.

North Korea and South Korea remain technically at war because the 1950–1953 Korean War ended in an armistice rather than a peace treaty.

World.title: US bars Fiji-based man over corruption tied to China
World.content:
The State Department has accused the official of paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance Chinese interests.

Share US bars Fiji-based man over corruption tied to China on social media

The US Department of State has publicly designated a Fiji-based man for his involvement in corruption on behalf of Chinese actors.

Zhao Fugang, the director of the Overseas Chinese Service Center, “abused his public position by paying bribes to Fijian citizens to advance China-based government, business, and criminal interests”, the State Department said in a press release on Wednesday.

“His actions constituted significant corruption and adversely affected U.S. interests in Fiji.”

The designation renders Zhao and his immediate family members “generally ineligible for entry into the United States”.

The US embassy in Suva, Fiji’s capital, said Zhao’s actions left the Pacific nation open to “malign foreign influence facilitated by Chinese government, business, and criminal actors”.

The embassy also said, “Public reporting shows an established trend of criminals operating across the Pacific with ties to China.”

Beijing says Overseas Chinese Service Centers help its nationals with administrative issues abroad, such as renewing driving licences. However, rights groups have alleged they are fronts for Beijing to push interests abroad, including the targeting of dissidents.

In February, the Trump administration sanctioned two leaders of Pacific island nations for alleged corruption tied to China. The US Department of State issued a notice alleging that Hokkons Baules, the president of Palau’s Senate, and Anderson Jibas, a former mayor in the Marshall Islands, had created openings for China to increase its influence in the region.

World.title: Tanker hit by multiple projectiles off north coast of Qatar, UKMTO says
World.content:
British maritime agency has recently reported a rise in attacks on vessels in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz.

Share Tanker hit by multiple projectiles off north coast of Qatar, UKMTO says on social media

A number of casualties have been reported after a tanker sailing off the north coast of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency has announced.

The vessel was hit by several projectiles 94 kilometres (58 miles) north of Madinat ash Shamal, UKMTO said on Wednesday. The incident comes as the British maritime agency reported a recent rise in attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz.

UKMTO did not say how many people were killed or injured in this latest attack, adding that authorities were investigating. It did not specify the origin of the ship.

An attack on a vessel in the middle of the Gulf is unusual. The Maritime Executive, a publication specialising in commercial shipping, said it was the first reported attack on a tanker in the western half of the Gulf in weeks.

Qatar has not commented on the reported attack, which falls within its exclusive economic zone.

Vessels have more commonly been targeted in the strategically important Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway linking the Gulf with the Gulf of Oman.

Before the United States-Israel war on Iran began on February 28, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessels a day, and shipments through it accounted for about 20 percent of global crude and liquefied natural gas supplies.

In retaliation for US-Israeli attacks, Iran effectively closed the strait, while Washington has maintained a blockade on Iranian ports.

UKMTO said on Tuesday that there had been nine attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz this month, representing half of the September total in the waterway and the Gulf combined.



Despite the attacks, oil exports from the Middle East have risen to, and according to provisional data even surpassed, pre-war levels in recent weeks.

The seven-day moving average of Middle East crude exports reached 18.3 million barrels per day (bpd) on September 30, compared with about 18 million bpd on average in the 12 months before the war, according to Kpler, a data firm.

World.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
World.content:
A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity, external is being bankrolled and protected by the US and Lebanese authorities, a BBC News investigation has found.

Bassam al-Hassan, who oversaw Syria's chemical weapons programme and was a senior adviser to former President Bashar al-Assad, is being harboured in Lebanon following the Assad regime's collapse in 2024.

An investigation by the BBC and the US broadcaster NPR has discovered that Hassan has been allowed to remain there under an arrangement involving the FBI, and other US and Lebanese authorities. This is because of his willingness to provide information about the abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria in 2012, as well as additional intelligence, we have been told.

Last month the BBC revealed Tice's abduction had been a planned operation, with Hassan in the chain of command.

Officials from two different branches of Syria's new government have told the BBC they want Hassan returned to face trial, but that US authorities want him kept in Lebanon, and they say there is little Damascus can do about this.

We asked the FBI, the CIA and Lebanon's General Directorate of General Security to comment on our findings. Only the FBI responded, declining to comment and instead directing us to a past statement that said its focus remained on establishing the facts around the Tice case and securing his return.

In response to our findings, Phil Elwood, spokesperson for the Tice family said: "If what you are saying is true, the fact that our tax dollars are being used to furnish a comfortable life for someone associated with the use of chemical weapons on Syrian civilians, who claims to have had Austin Tice executed, is offensive.

"This is nothing less than aiding and abetting the escape of a wanted war criminal. The Syrians deserve justice and he should be returned to stand trial."

World.title: Texas carries out first US execution since Christa Pike's botched lethal injections
World.content:
A death row inmate was executed by lethal injection on Wednesday evening in Texas, the first execution in the US since the failed attempt to put Christa Pike to death last week.

Lawyers for 46-year-old Jamaal Howard had asked a judge to pause the execution in light of Pike's botched injections last week, according to the BBC's US partner, CBS News.

But courts denied their requests, and he received a fatal dose of pentobarbital at the state prison in Huntsville. He was pronounced dead at 20:03 local time.

Howard was convicted and sentenced to death for the 2000 murder of a convenience store clerk during a robbery he committed.

His lawyers had argued that because Texas planned to inject Howard with the same drug - pentobarbital - that was used on Pike, he faced the same risks. They also alleged that Texas' supply of the drug had become degraded, as Pike's lawyers have similarly argued.

A court twice denied their appeals and the US Supreme Court also turned down the appeal late Wednesday.

"Texas should not be eager to follow in Tennessee's footsteps; a stay would keep that from happening," Howard's attorneys had argued, CBS reported.

Howard's attorneys also asked Texas Governor Greg Abbott, a Republican, to delay the execution by 30 days so they could seek additional information about the drug used in the execution. The governor did not grant the delay.

Howard was 20 when he shot Vickie Swartout, 42, who was working at a convenience store in Texas. Howard stole a carton of cigarettes and $114 from the register.

Asked if he had a final statement before his execution, Howard apologized to Swartout's family, who watched from a witness room, US media report.

"I wish that you accept my apology, and I wish for your forgiveness," Howard said. "I'm sorry for what happened. I wish you can learn to forgive me one of these days."

World.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
World.content:
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.

Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford rent increases.

The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.

"We regret to announce that Maricarmen passed away today," the Madrid Tenants' Union said in a statement, adding her situation marked "a turning point in the history of this country".

Union spokesperson Alicia del RÃ­o said: "Speculation costs lives, and today rentierism has finished killing our colleague Maricarmen" but "her memory lives on with us".

A cause of death was not announced.

Abascal's death was received in Puerta del Sol - a square in Madrid where thousands have been camping since Abascal's eviction last month to demand more affordable housing - with a collective gasp followed by a minute of silence.

Dozens of candles were lit around the square while more candles formed an altar to Abascal in front of the headquarters of the Community of Madrid government.

Messages on cardboard banners read "it's not a death, it's a killing", "the fight will continue" and "Mari Carmen, the grandmother of the whole country", among others.
