World.title: India exposes Pakistan’s doublespeak at UN, says world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11, Pahalgam attacks
World.content:
Exposing Pakistan’s doublespeak on terrorism at the UN, India has called out Islamabad’s efforts to gloss over its state support for terror by announcing rewards for Jaish-e-Mohammad (JeM) chief Masood Azahar, underlining that the world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam attacks.

India on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) exercised its Right of Reply in response to the Pakistan representative’s statement in the Sixth Committee of the UN General Assembly on the Agenda Item: Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism.

“Pakistan speaks of combating terrorism while seeking to obscure the very question that this committee must confront — What happens when terrorists are financed, facilitated, trained, sheltered, or supported from the territory of a State?,” First Secretary in the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Raghoo Puri said.

He said India has been consistent on this question, underscoring that terrorism cannot be defeated by declarations and instead requires action against its perpetrators, organisers, financiers, and sponsors.

“For years, Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline State in combating terrorism and as a victim while masking the fact that the Frankensteins the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan,” Mr. Puri said.

Calling out Pakistan’s doublespeak on terrorism, Mr. Puri said the country “glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country, Masood Azhar.”

He said the world is aware of Pakistan's financial support to terrorism.

“Yet, we also remember that just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation. The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different,” he said.

Mr. Puri said that when the media can reach Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, "surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts”.

In May last year, India had launched Operation Sindoor targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the dastardly April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir perpetrated by The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists were killed.

Earlier this month, India had dismissed as “gimmicks” Pakistan’s fresh announcement of a bounty of seven million rupees on Azhar, demanding that Islamabad take “concrete action” to combat terrorism.

India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar, while Pakistan has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan — a claim rejected by Afghanistan’s Taliban government.

For the last few years, Islamabad has claimed that the JeM founder has been operating from Afghanistan.

However, the Taliban regime dismissed Pakistan’s repeated claims, with a senior Afghan Foreign Ministry official saying he is not in the country.

Islamabad’s fresh announcement on the reward for information on Azhar came as it faces pressure from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) to crack down on terror groups and their leadership.

The Paris-based global watchdog is set to review Pakistan’s anti-terrorism efforts at its upcoming plenary.

Pakistan was placed under the FATF grey list between 2018 and 2022 for its systemic deficiencies in anti-money laundering and its failure to counter-terror financing.

Mr. Puri also recalled a recent statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, daughter of former Pakistan Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, who had said, “The unfortunate thing is that the threat [Punjab] faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces.”

Exposing this “dark secret”, Mr. Puri said, “You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds. Reality never works like that.”

“When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice,” he said.

“The world has not forgotten 9/11 and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught. The world has not forgotten 26/11. The world has not forgotten Pahalgam,” Mr. Puri said, adding that the list, “unfortunately”, is painfully long.

“The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation, they were asked about their religion. It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism,” he said.

“Pakistan continues with its narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation. If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are of course welcome to enjoy it," Mr. Puri said.

"Any regime against terrorism to be effective must do two things — assign responsibility and ensure accountability. India will defend its people, and continued terrorism against India will have consequences,” he added.

In another Right of Reply, Mr. Puri said India rejected Pakistan’s “circular economy” of words and narratives.

“If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place. But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government,” he said, referring to a term used to describe allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.

World.title: JNTU-GV students can now get certificates online in days, without ₹3,000 tatkal fee
World.content:
Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University-Gurajada, Vizianagaram (JNTU-GV) Vice-Chancellor V.V. Subba Rao on Thursday (October 8, 2026) said the university had introduced student-centric governance so that students could get all services without hassle. He said students no longer needed to pay a ₹3,000 tatkal fee to quickly obtain their original degrees and other certificates from the university.

The new online system would help them get certificates in a couple of days, and there was no need for them to visit the university and submit applications offline, he said. The statutory fees for each service can be paid online.

Speaking to The Hindu here, he said the new initiative would benefit nearly 90,000 students studying in 37 affiliated colleges in six north Andhra districts, including Visakhapatnam and Srikakulam. “Earlier, the students used to face many difficulties with the submission of applications in offline mode. They used to come to JNTU-GV to know the status of their applications. Now, the offline procedure was stopped to ensure transparency in the administration,” he added.

Mr. Subba Rao, who completed one year as Vice-Chancellor on Wednesday (October 7, 2026), said the Centralised Academic Platform (CAP) mobile app had become another advantage for faculty members and students of the university colleges. All services related to academics, documents, hostel services and others could be accessed through the app, developed by the university recently, he said.

World.title: FIR against MLA for creating false death certificates of voters in Vijayapura
World.content:
Vijayapura police have registered an FIR against Basanagouda Patil Yatnal, MLA, on the charge of creating false death certificates of voters in a bid to exclude them from the voting list in Vijayapura Assembly constituency in Karnataka. Mr. Yatnal was expelled by the BJP in March 2025.

Officers of the Jala Nagar police station registered an FIR based on a complaint by Abdul Razak Bagwan, a vegetable vendor.

Mr. Bagwan has alleged that Mr. Yatnal, MLA and the Booth level agent of Vijayapura Assembly constituency, had falsely claimed that he had died, and that his name needs to be struck off the electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. Mr. Yatnal had managed to obtain a false death certificate through unfair means, the complainant alleged.

The complainant told the police that he knew of at least seven other persons who Mr. Yatnal had falsely claimed as dead, and had obtained false death certificates for all of them as part of a conspiracy to delete their names by submitting Form 7 against their inclusion in the voter list.

On October 7, members of the Vijayapura district unit of Mata Kavalu Samiti held a press meet in Bengaluru where persons who were passed off as deceased were presented before mediapersons.

The victims had submitted a memorandum in this regard to the DC and DEO of Vijayapura a week ago.

Activist Prakash Raj had raised this issue at a rally in Vijayapura a few days ago.

On October 7, eight Muslim women from Vijayapura alleged that they were wrongly shown as ‘deceased’ in documents submitted to the Election Commission of India (ECI) as part of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka. They demanded registration of a criminal case against Vijayapura MLA Basanagouda Patil Yatnal, and those responsible for submitting the alleged bogus death certificates.

The women made the allegations in Bengaluru at a press conference by Jagrutha Karnataka, a social-political organisation. They displayed copies of the death certificates and other documents which, they claimed, had been used to pass them off as dead.

Representatives of Jagrutha Karnataka alleged Mr. Yatnal had submitted the list in a letter dated August 31, a week after the publication of the draft electoral rolls on August 24. They questioned how names of voters across 198 polling stations could have been matched with details of deceased persons within one week.

They also questioned how colour photographs from voter ID cards accompanying the list had been obtained, alleging that such photographs were available in the ECI records.

‘People’s Tribunal’ in Bengaluru

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) announced a ‘People’s Tribunal’ on October 8 at Freedom Park in Bengaluru to allow voters across Karnataka to share grievances regarding wrongful removal from electoral lists.

On October 7, actor-activist Prakash Raj urged people to join the protest. “Tomorrow. 8th October, Bengaluru Freedom Park. There is going to be a state-level tribunal where victims of SIR, who are the evidences, will come across the State, to Bangalore Freedom Park. All the cockroaches, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, and all the young youth organisations and the civil society of Karnataka will be there,” he posted on X

The CJP has called people to Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on October 10 to press for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the controversy surrounding the SIR. The party has called for criminal action against Mr. Kumar.

Earlier on October 6, CJP founder Abhijit Dipke had criticised the Maharashtra Police for allegedly sending notices to CJP workers. He said the workers were being pressured to stay away from the October 10 protest to be held at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

World.title: RBI removes Paytm Payments Bank from list of scheduled banks
World.content:
The Reserve Bank has officially removed Paytm Payments Bank Ltd (PPBL) from the list of recognised scheduled banks following the cancellation of its banking licence.

In April this year, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had cancelled the banking licence issued to PPBL for non-compliance with norms, saying affairs of the bank were conducted in a manner detrimental to the interest of its depositors.

Later, the Delhi High Court ordered that PPBL be wound up.

"Paytm Payments Bank Limited has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934...," the central bank said in a statement on Wednesday (October 7, 2026).

A notification in this regard was published on July 31 and published in the Gazette of India in September.

The Second Schedule of the RBI Act is the official list of recognised banks that meet the central bank's financial standards and get special operational privileges. 'Scheduled bank' means a bank included in the Second Schedule.

PPBL, an associate firm of Vijay Shekhar Sharma-promoted fintech firm Paytm, came under the regulatory scanner on multiple occasions earlier, including in March 2022 when the central bank barred it from onboarding new customers.

While cancelling the licence, the RBI had said the affairs of the bank were conducted in a manner detrimental to its own interests as well as its depositors.

Earlier, PPBL was directed to stop onboarding new customers with effect from March 11, 2022 amid "material supervisory concerns" observed in the bank.

The bank was also directed to appoint an IT audit firm to conduct a comprehensive system audit of its IT system.

Thereafter, on January 31, 2024 and February 16, 2024, certain business restrictions were also imposed on the bank, including disallowing any further deposits/credits/ top-ups in existing customer accounts, prepaid instruments, and wallets.

World.title: Four Bengal workers, detained on Bangladeshi suspicion, released from Chhattisgarh
World.content:
After the Calcutta High Court’s intervention, Chhattisgarh Police have released the four migrant workers from West Bengal, who had been detained for over a month on suspicion of being Bangladeshi nationals.

On Monday (October 5, 2026), the Calcutta HC questioned the Foreigners Registration Officer (FRO), who is also the Superintendent of Police, Chhattisgarh’s Bilaspur, over the authority’s move to determine the citizenship of four men from Murshidabad while their appeals against deletion of their names from the electoral roll during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) are pending before the appellate tribunal.

It also rapped the Chhattisgarh State for its ‘double standard’. It said that the situation was ‘contradictory’. “If the authorities were saying that some persons were not Indian citizens, then what would the appellate authority (tribunal) do?” questioned Justice Krishna Rao.

It asked the Election Commission whether it was “playing” with the persons. The Supreme Court has formed the tribunal to decide on appeals by those whose names have been deleted from the electoral rolls. The court asked how the FRRO could make a decision on their citizenship.

Now, the night before the next hearing of the case on Thursday (October 8, 2026), all four of them- Sabir Sheikh (42), Safikul Islam (39), Nasiruddin Sheikh (35), and Laltu Sheikh (28)- have been released from the holding centre at around 9 pm on Wednesday (October 7, 2026).

“We were so surprised. It happened suddenly when we lost our hope. We finished out dinner and went to the security personnel at the gate to mark our attendance. But they suddenly told us that we don’t need to do it anymore. The higher authority ordered them to release us immediately. The Police also wrote it in the order copy that we are Indians, not Bangladeshis,” said Safikul over a phone call.

These four men were part of a group of 23 such migrant workers- mostly from Murshidabad’s Samserganj and Sahabad areas, went to Chhattisgarh in search of work, where they have also been selling goods house-to-house in the Bilaspur area.

On September 4, Chhattisgarh police detained at least 23 of them from their residences in Chunchiapara-Ganesh Nagar under Sirgiti police station on suspicion of being Bangladeshi nationals. They were initially taken to the Bilaspur Police Superintendent’s office, from where they were moved to a holding centre in Raipur for illegal immigrants.

Later, 19 out of 23 of these labourers have been released on September 18, 2026 after the local civil court’s order while these four continued to be at the detention centre. The police, in the court, questioned their nationality based on the deletion of their names in the special intensive revision (SIR). To be sure, the rest of the 19 found their names back to the voter list after the adjudication process in April while these four were left off.

They have now appealed before the tribunal seeking restoration of their names. However, the applications are still pending.

Meanwhile, the Chhattisgarh administration had sought a verification report from the Murshidabad district magistrate, but the report was reportedly not provided by the West Bengal administration. As a result, the families were compelled to approach the Calcutta High Court.

The petitioners said that they were detained even when their appeals against the deletion of their names from the electoral rolls are pending before the tribunal. Therefore, the actions taken by the authorities are “wholly arbitrary, illegal, and unsustainable in law”. They have temporarily visited Chhattisgarh for work but have ‘permanent roots’ in West Bengal.

Reacting to the development, the Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP, Samirul Islam, urged the bureaucrats not to delay in such verification reports of the citizens sought by another administration. He asked them to execute it with a sense of responsibility to protect the rights and interests of every citizen without any ‘political considerations’.

“District magistrates and other officials are expected to serve the people of their districts impartially. Helping citizens in such circumstances is not a favour; it is an administrative responsibility. In this case, the absence of timely administrative assistance left the families with no option but to seek judicial intervention. I thank the judiciary, which is the place of our last hope,” he said on X.

World.title: Andhra Pradesh declares early kharif drought in 388 mandals across 21 districts
World.content:
The Andhra Pradesh government has declared an early kharif 2026 drought in 388 mandals across 21 districts, classifying 283 mandals as severely drought-affected and 105 as moderately drought-affected, citing a 53.4% rainfall deficit during June-August and prevailing El Niño conditions.

More than 56% of the State’s 688 mandals in 28 districts have been declared drought-affected.

The declaration was made through G.O. Ms. No. 4, published by G. Sai Prasad, Special Chief Secretary (FAC), Revenue (Disaster Management) Department, on October 1, 2026, following detailed scrutiny of proposals submitted by district Collectors and recommendations of the State Drought Committee. The committee met on September 30 and assessed the proposals in accordance with the Government of India’s Manual for Drought Management, 2016.

The government said an average rainfall of only 197.6 mm was recorded between June 1 and August 31, against a normal of 424.3 mm. Although the kharif drought declaration is normally required by October 31, the government opted for an early declaration based on the rainfall situation and relevant drought indicators.

The assessment followed three stages: mandatory indicators, including rainfall deviation and dry spells; impact indicators, comprising sown-area index, Remote Sensing/Vegetation Condition Index, Moisture Adequacy Index, Reservoir Storage Index and Ground Water Index; and ground truthing.

Rainfall deviation was classified as normal at +19% to -19%, deficient at -20% to -59%, large deficient/scanty at -60% to -99% and no rain at -100%. A dry spell was defined as a period of three to four consecutive weeks of low or no rainfall, depending on soil type.

Data for the assessment was sourced from the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, the Agriculture and Horticulture departments, the Andhra Pradesh Space Applications Centre (APSAC), the Irrigation Department, the Ground Water Audit Department and Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU).

District-wise, the affected mandals comprise Srikakulam (1 severe, 4 moderate), Vizianagaram (10, 12), Visakhapatnam (1, 3), Anakapalli (22, 0), Kakinada (0, 6), East Godavari (0, 4), Eluru (1, 7), Krishna (8, 9), NTR (3, 10), Guntur (8, 3), Bapatla (15, 0), Palnadu (18, 10), Prakasam (18, 10), Markapuram (19, 0), Kurnool (15, 0), Nandyal (26, 2), Ananthapuramu (27, 1), Sri Sathya Sai (28, 1), YSR Kadapa (14, 23), Annamayya (25, 0) and Chittoor (24, 0).

District Collectors have been directed to publish notifications in the respective District Gazettes in English and Telugu and specify the affected mandals.

World.title: At least two fresh FIRs against Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi over alleged assault on cops, police vehicle vandalism
World.content:
At least two fresh FIRs have been registered against Congress leaders, including Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, in connection with the INDIA bloc’s protest in central Delhi on Wednesday (October 7, 2026) against the revision of electoral rolls and demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Delhi Police sources said.

CEC row LIVE: October 8, 2026

The latest cases relate to allegations of assaulting and obstructing police personnel deployed during the protest and damaging a police vehicle, a police source close to the matter told The Hindu. The police are also registering another case over the staging of an unauthorised protest.

The FIRs are separate from the cases registered following the INDIA bloc’s protest on Tuesday (October 6, 2026). Police had earlier booked Opposition leaders in connection with the previous demonstration, including over forcible entry (or criminal trespass) into Akashvani Bhavan.

The fresh cases were registered after a police constable deployed for crowd control alleged that he was surrounded and assaulted by protesters during Wednesday’s (October 7, 2026) demonstration.

The constable, identified as Ankit Kasana and posted with the Parliament Police, told the police that a group of around 30 to 35 protesters, including men and women, surrounded him while the police were trying to manage the crowd during Mr. Gandhi’s detention. He alleged that the protesters abused him, tore his uniform and attacked him with their fingernails and teeth.

Mr. Kasana was subsequently taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital for a medical examination.

“The FIR was lodged after the statement of the personnel who were assaulted during the protest,” a police official said.

Police alleged that protesters damaged a police vehicle, smashing its windows, during Wednesday’s (October 9, 2026) demonstration, while Congress workers punctured the tyre of a bus carrying detained protesters.

Wednesday’s action came after another day of confrontation between the Opposition and the Delhi Police over the INDIA bloc’s campaign against the revision of electoral rolls. The Opposition parties have been demanding the removal of Mr. Kumar, alleging that the electoral roll revision process is being carried out without adequate safeguards and transparency. The Election Commission has rejected the Opposition’s allegations.

On Wednesday (October 7, 2026), Mr. Gandhi, Ms. Vadra and around 80 other leaders were detained by the New Delhi police after the protesters gathered in the Jantar Mantar area. The police pushed the protesters into buses and took them away.

Congress workers allegedly punctured a tyre of one of the buses being used to transport the protesters. Videos of the incident went viral on social media platforms. Mr. Gandhi was subsequently moved to another bus and taken to a police station on Barakhamba Road, where he remained in detention for several hours before being released.

Congress leaders K.C. Venugopal, Pawan Khera, A.A. Rahim and Sivadasan were among those detained along with the Gandhis.

A senior police official said the force had observed a growing pattern of “competition” among organisations staging protests, with groups increasingly seeking to make their demonstrations more dramatic and attract greater attention. “There is now a competition between the various organisations staging protests to make them more dramatic and damage public property to get more attention,” the official said.

Another INDIA bloc protest has been planned for Thursday (October 8, 2026), prompting the Delhi Police to reinforce security arrangements across central Delhi. Barricades have been placed at several points and additional personnel deployed at locations expected to witness gatherings.

Police officials said those found violating the law during Thursday’s demonstration would be detained and cases registered.

The successive protests have resulted in major traffic restrictions and heightened police presence in the heart of the capital.

World.title: Pakistan, IMF reach staff-level agreement for $1.2bn tranche
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Thursday reached a staff-level agreement (SLA) with the Pakistani authorities on the fourth review under the $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review under the $1.4bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF), qualifying Pakistan to draw about $1.2bn from the Fund’s resources within four to five weeks.

“The IMF team has reached an SLA with the Pakistani authorities on the fourth review of the 37-month Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and the third review of the 28-month arrangement under the Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF)”, the lending agency announced in an early morning statement.

The SLA is subject to approval by the IMF Executive Board. Upon approval, Pakistan will have access to about $1bn (SDR 760 million) under the EFF and about $210 million (SDR 154 million) under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to about $5.7bn, it said.

The two sides also concluded Article IV consultations, the IMF announced from Washington headquarters.

“Program implementation under the EFF has remained broadly on track despite a challenging external environment. The authorities remain committed to preserving macroeconomic stability, strengthening public finances, ensuring that inflation returns durably to the State Bank of Pakistan’s target range, enhancing energy sector viability, strengthening social protection, and accelerating reforms to foster sustainable, private sector-led, and inclusive growth,” the IMF statement said.

The authorities have also continued to advance their climate reform agenda under the RSF to strengthen Pakistan’s resilience and reduce vulnerabilities to climate-related risks, it added.

The fund team led by Iva Petrova was in Pakistan and held discussions under the 2026 Article IV consultation and on the 4th review EFF and the 3rd review under the RSF from September 23 to October 7.

“Supported by the EFF, the authorities have successfully navigated the impact of the Middle East conflict, and strong policies have helped preserve macroeconomic stability. Real GDP growth reached 4 per cent in the first three quarters of FY26, and although higher energy prices and supply disruptions weakened somewhat the momentum, FY26 growth is estimated at 3.6pc.”

Headline inflation moderated to about 10.3pc in September after peaking in May, while core inflation remained contained, the fund said.

It added: “The current account was broadly balanced in FY26 supported by strong remittances, and gross reserves rose to about $21.5bn by end-September. Sovereign rating upgrades and renewed international market access also point to stronger policy credibility. Nevertheless, the fund said risks remain high, particularly from geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices, tighter global financial conditions, and trade disruptions.”

The authorities remain committed to sound macroeconomic policies, which are critical to safeguarding stability amidst the ongoing shock-prone environment, it further stated.

The authorities’ policy priorities would continue to maintain strong fiscal policies. Steadfast implementation of the FY27 budget, anchored by an underlying primary surplus of 2pc of GDP and supported by tax policy and revenue administration measures, is critical to placing public debt on a durable downward path, it noted.

Revenue administration reforms, including improved risk-based audits, digital invoicing, and use of third-party data, will help safeguard the revenue targets. A comprehensive medium-term tax reform strategy should make the system fairer, simpler, and more growth-friendly, while protecting revenues and reducing distortions, the statement said.

The authorities will stay the course in enhancing public financial management, it said, noting that they were “making progress in strengthening public financial management to improve the efficiency and transparency of the budget process, public investment, procurement, and government cash management.

“They remain committed to reducing debt rollover risks and servicing costs amid elevated gross financing needs, while advancing the development of the domestic government securities market and diversifying the investor base,” the IMF said.

On social protections, the IMF said authorities had arrested the long-term decline in health and education spending, raising it from 2.2pc of GDP in FY24 to 2.5pc of GDP in FY26.

It noted that the authorities were “committed to increasing it further to 2.8pc of GDP in FY27, closely monitoring implementation, and reallocating resources as needed to meet this objective.

“The planned increase in targeted cash-transfer benefits, together with continued improvements in beneficiary coverage and payment systems, will strengthen protection for vulnerable households and support more inclusive growth.”

The fund called for phasing out the fuel support scheme promptly, given its high cost and broad targeting. Any future fuel support—should oil prices surprise on the upside—should be limited, time-bound, targeted using established social assistance programs, and accommodated within the FY27 budget envelope, it said.

It called on the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) to maintain an “appropriately tight” policy stance to ensure inflation returns durably to the SBP’s target range.

“Exchange rate flexibility should continue to serve as an important shock absorber, while further reserve accumulation, gradual liberalisation of the foreign exchange regime, and deeper domestic financial markets will strengthen resilience and support private sector development,” it directed.

The fund also called for timely tariff adjustments and cost-reducing reforms essential to prevent renewed circular debt accumulation while protecting vulnerable consumers.

“Priorities include improving sector efficiency, advancing private participation in distribution, deepening electricity market competition, maintaining gas sector cost recovery, and reducing unaccounted-for gas losses”, it said.

The fund said that Article IV consultation focused on reforms to support the structural transformation of the economy to higher value-added activities and reduce gaps relative to peer countries in key areas, including by strengthening competition, reducing regulatory and trade barriers, advancing privatisation, enhancing SOE governance and transparency, and strengthening governance and anti-corruption institutions.

Together with efforts to introduce a simpler and fairer tax system, allocate greater public resources toward human and capital development, ensure a more cost-efficient energy sector, and deepen financial markets, these reforms are critical to raise productivity, increase labour force participation and job creation, and support private investment and exports, it noted.

“Supported by the RSF, the authorities are continuing efforts to strengthen resilience to climate change, with recent progress in mainstreaming climate considerations into public investment planning and strengthening disaster risk financing and coordination.

“Further reforms are advancing on irrigation water pricing and collection, better-targeted electricity subsidies, energy-efficiency standards, and transport decarbonization.”

Later in the day, the Ministry of Finance, in a post on social media platform X, said that Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb held a “wrap-up session” with Petrova at the conclusion of the review.

EFF and RSF packages

Pakis­tan and the IMF had reached the 39-month $7bn aid package deal in July 2024, with the programme set to allow the country to “cement macroeconomic stability and create conditions for stronger, more inclusive and resilient growth”.

In March 2025, the two sides reached an SLA on the first biannual review of the EFF programme and on unlocking the $1.3bn RSF arrangement.

Subsequently, in May that year, the IMF’s Executive Board allowed a $1bn disbursement under the EFF — bringing total released funds under the package to about $2.1bn — and also approved the RSF loan.

In October 2025, the government and the Fund reached an SLA on the second review of the EFF, securing another $1bn under the programme and $200 million under the RSF after the Board’s approval in December.

A Petrova-led mission held talks with Pakistan in March this year for the third review of the EFF and the second review of the RSF, but the two sides failed to reach an agreement and decided to continue negotiations.

Then in May, the IMF’s Executive Board allowed Pakistan to draw about $1.1bn under the EFF and about $220m under the RSF, bringing total disbursements under the two arrangements to roughly $4.8bn.

World.title: 9 terrorists killed in North Waziristan IBO: state media
World.content:
Security forces killed nine terrorists in an intelligence-based operation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan, state media reported on Wednesday.

According to state-run Pakistan TV, IBOs were carried out in several areas of North Waziristan, including Palangzai, Nadeem Kot, and Kot Khazri, eliminating nine Fitna al-Khwarij terrorists, including four “important terrorist commanders”.

Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

It added that several hideouts were destroyed and a large quantity of weapons and ammunition was recovered from the slain terrorists.

KP has long faced security challenges. In August, the province, excluding the merged districts, recorded 54 terrorist attacks compared with 36 in July, representing an increase of 50 per cent, according to data compiled by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS).

A day earlier, security forces killed 13 terrorists in another IBO in North Waziristan. On Tuesday, in yet another North Waziristan IBO, security forces killed five terrorists, state media said, while seven were killed on October 2.

On September 30, security forces killed three terrorists in an IBO in Mir Ali. A day before that, in an IBO in the Bara area, security forces killed five terrorists. On Sept 28, four terrorists were killed during an IBO in Dera Ismail Khan.

On Sept 26, a dozen people lost their lives while 35 others were injured in a suicide blast that targeted the Aman Mela police checkpost in DI Khan’s Darazinda tehsil. On Sept 18, a major attack in the old Police Lines in Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others.

World.title: Trump says he deserves Nobel Peace Prize but has doubts he will get it
World.content:
US President Donald Trump, who waged war with Iran and has yet to broker peace in Ukraine, said on Wednesday that he should win the Nobel Peace Prize but acknowledged doubt about his chances.

“I don’t know what their decision is going to be,” Trump said of the 2026 award, which the Norwegian Nobel Committee will announce on Friday.

“They have a reputation for maybe not giving it to people like me.” Since his return to the White House last year, Trump has repeatedly said he deserves what may be the world’s most prestigious award.

“It is about that time,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “But I was very honoured to receive it indirectly last time by the recipient, who said nobody in history deserves it more than President Trump.” Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gave her 2025 Nobel Peace Prize medal to Trump in January as she sought US support for her efforts in Venezuela.

Trump said he should get the prize after wading into eight conflicts since taking office last January.

The leaders of Cambodia, Israel and Pakistan have said they nominated Trump, though there is no way of verifying that.

Parties to some conflicts Trump claims to have resolved dispute the US president’s diplomatic role, and fighting has flared again in some of those regions, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and along the border between Cambodia and Thailand.

A resolution to Russia’s war in Ukraine has eluded Trump, who promised to end it on the first day of his second White House term. US-Israel strikes on Iran have led to a seven-month simmering conflict that has upended global energy supplies and driven gas prices up before November’s midterm elections.

Pope Leo, the International Criminal Court, and the special rapporteur for the Palestinian Territories are among the favourites to win this year.

World.title: El Nino will intensify, then peak in December: UN
World.content:
El Nino will intensify even more before peaking in December, the United Nations said Thursday, warning it could be among the strongest witnessed since at least 1950.

The naturally occurring weather phenomenon is set to bring higher temperatures to much of the planet, the UN’s weather and climate agency said, with its impact compounding the effects of man-made climate change.

“El Nino will continue to intensify ahead of its forecast peak in December,” the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in its monthly Global Seasonal Climate Update.

“It is likely to bring above-average temperatures to much of the globe and shift rainfall patterns, increasing the risk of drought and floods in different regions.” El Nino warms surface temperatures in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean, bringing worldwide changes in winds, pressure and rainfall patterns.

It typically takes place every two to seven years and lasts around nine to 12 months.

Conditions oscillate between El Nino and its opposite La Nina, with neutral conditions in between.

El Nino ‘strengthening rapidly’

“Sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific are forecast to increase to record levels during October-November-December 2026, reflecting the strengthening of the El Nino event which will drive weather patterns and impact economies, ecosystems and communities across the globe,” the WMO said.

The forecast is based on consensus across 13 leading national and international meteorological centres.

“El Nino is firmly established and strengthening rapidly,” said WMO chief Celeste Saulo.

“WMO forecasts indicate a near-100 per cent likelihood that it will persist through February 2027, potentially being one of the strongest since at least 1950.” Saulo explained that El Nino does not add new heat to the planet, but releases heat being stored in the ocean.

“The ocean it’s drawing from is the warmest we’ve ever measured it. There is simply more heat available to release,” she said.

Sea temperatures record

The index which measures sea surface temperature anomalies across the central-eastern equatorial Pacific — the region at the heart of El Nino — increased from 1.6°C above normal in June to 2.5°C above normal in August.

For October-November-December, the anomaly is forecast to reach approximately 3.7°C above normal.

This would be the highest since observations began, eclipsing the previous record of 2.6°C set in 2015-2016.

The last El Nino contributed to making 2023 the second-hottest year on record and 2024 the all-time high at around 1.55°C above the 1850-1900 pre-industrial average.

While El Nino usually peaks between November and February, the resulting spike in temperatures typically comes later.

This El Nino is already hitting some regions hard, including in Central America, where animals and crops are dying from drought.

World.title: PCB confirms window for HBL PSL 12
World.content:
The 12th edition of the HBL Pakistan Super League will be held from March 18 to May 2 next year, the Pakistan Cricket Board announced on Thursday.

The window was finalised following consultations with the owners and representatives of the eight franchises at a meeting of the PSL governing council in London on Sept 1, according to the PCB.

The board said details of the schedule, venues and ticketing arrangements would be announced later, while the next phase of squad-building will include direct signings, player retentions, a trade window and the player auction.

PSL 12 will follow an expanded 2026 season in which the league featured eight teams for the first time following the addition of Hyderabad Kingsmen and the Rawalpindiz franchises. The 2026 edition also saw the PSL move from the draft system to a player auction for the first time.

The inaugural auction, held in February, saw 103 players sold to the eight franchises. The PCB had subsequently said that players retained or acquired at the auction would be on two-year contracts covering the 11th and 12th editions, with franchises allowed to retain up to seven players for the next season.

The 2026 season ended with Peshawar Zalmi claiming their second PSL title after defeating debutants Hyderabad Kingsmen by five wickets in the final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on May 3.

PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi said the previous edition had set a high benchmark for the league.

“HBL PSL 11 showed the world what this league is capable of – thrilling moments that had the whole nation transfixed, record crowds, record broadcasts,” he was quoted as saying in a PCB press release. “HBL PSL 12 will raise the bar further.

“We are committed to delivering another outstanding season and look forward to seeing all eight franchises compete once again for the title,” he added.

PSL chief executive Salman Naseer said Thursday’s announcement was the beginning of preparations for the next season.

“Last season changed what people expect from this league and we intend to meet every one of those expectations in 2027,” he said.

“Direct signings, retentions, the trade window and the auction will each bring their own excitement in the months ahead,” he added.

The eight franchises — Islamabad United, Karachi Kings, Lahore Qalandars, Multan Sultans, Peshawar Zalmi, Quetta Gladiators, Hyderabad Kingsmen and Rawalpindiz — will now begin preparing for the new season as the PCB works towards finalising the schedule and squad-building process.

Further details on the venues, auction and ticketing arrangements will be announced by the PCB in due course

World.title: Govt raises petrol price by Rs1.82 per litre, reduces high-speed diesel rate by Re0.91
World.content:
The government on Wednesday raised the price of petrol by Rs1.82 per litre, but reduced that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.91 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs396.65 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs394.94 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 8 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: DG ISPR says Pakistani troops present in Saudi Arabia 'for decades' across multiple domains
World.content:
Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) Director General Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry has said that Pakistani troops are in Saudi Arabia, adding that they had been in the kingdom “for decades” and across multiple domains.

The military spokesperson made these remarks during an interview with CNN correspondent Ivan Watson, who posted a small clip on his X account.

“I can confirm that the forces of Pakistan are already there (Saudi Arabia),” Lt Gen Chaudhry said.

Watson then sought a confirmation that Pakistani troops were already on the ground in Saudi Arabia as part of the Makkah Defence Alliance between Pakistan, the kingdom and Turkiye.

To that, the military spokesperson replied, “Pakistan troops have been there for decades […] The Makkah alliance is not something that has come out in a vacuum. So there is a sustained diplomatic, political, military and people-to-people relationship between Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. So, I can share with you that Pakistani forces, in multiple capabilities and domains, are already there.”

Lt Gen Chaudhry’s remarks come after Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agreed to the deployment of military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom during an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh on Monday.

The three countries had held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia.

“The committee decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the kingdom, in accordance with the approved arrangements and the national legislation of the parties, thereby enhancing readiness, military integration, and the collective capacity to confront and counter threats,” a statement issued by the Foreign Office after the meeting said.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia in the Yemen conflict.

Separately, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who was part of Pakistan’s delegation in the meeting, joined Geo News programme ‘Aaj Shahzeb Khanzada Kay Saath’ via telephone the same day and said Saudi Arabia had made “gains and recovered some areas” in Yemen in the ongoing fighting with the Houthis.

When asked about a possible operational role by Pakistan and Turkiye, the defence minister replied that both nations had a “presence in theatre”, but only Saudi troops were involved in combat operations.

“Whatever assistance they require is being provided. But right now, the Turkish and Pakistani armies are playing a supportive role,” he said, noting that Pakistan was involved in reconnaissance.

Asif had earlier also reaffirmed that Pakistan would “practically and diplomatically” stand by Saudi Arabia against Yemen’s Houthi rebels if the situation escalated. The defence minister had said that Pakistan would fulfil all its obligations under the Makkah Defence Alliance in accordance with the terms of the agreement between the three countries.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

On Sept 25, the military chiefs of alliance members Pakistan, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia met in Riyadh for urgently convened talks under the pact in light of the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

World.title: Capital police bar officers, personnel from using social media
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The capital police have banned the use of social media for all ranks, including officers and other employees, and have warned that strict departmental action will be taken in accordance with the relevant rules in case of any violation.

In this regard, a policy was issued by the office of the police chief, Islamabad, bearing the signature of the deputy inspector general of police headquarters.

According to the policy, all officers and officials, along with other staff, are directed not to speak at public forums in their official capacity, publish articles in print media, or express opinions or issue official statements on social media platforms without prior permission.

Making videos or taking photographs while wearing a police uniform, whether in the premises of government buildings, vehicles or other private places for personal publicity or glorification is strictly prohibited.

Furthermore, the policy restricts officers or officials from uploading, sharing, or disseminating any confidential or official document, photograph or their content on social media or any other media platform.

Under this policy, the officers shall not share or express personal political or religious views on any media platform. Official channels for disseminating information regarding police activities shall be operated exclusively by the public relations branch, central police office.

Unit heads shall be responsible for personally supervising and monitoring the activities of all officers and officials posted in their respective divisions, zones and units. In case of any violation, strict departmental action shall be taken in accordance with the relevant rules.

The policy shall be implemented with immediate effect and shall remain in force until further orders. Officers, officials and personnel of all ranks shall ensure strict compliance with this policy.

Published in Dawn, October 8th, 2026
